meta_data.content:
# Narrative Templates

**Brand Origin Story:** The story of graph8 begins inside CIENCE — a company that spent a decade running real B2B outbound campaigns at scale for thousands of companies, including brands like Okta, Google, Microsoft, Uber, Salesforce, and Segment. After running millions of outbound touches and booking meetings across 2,500+ B2B brands, the team arrived at a painful and undeniable insight: the revenue stack was fundamentally broken.

The problem wasn't effort. Revenue teams were working hard. The problem was architecture. Every team was stitching together eight, ten, sometimes twelve disconnected point tools — a data vendor here, a sequencer there, a dialer somewhere else, a CRM that barely talked to any of them, a CDP bolted on for good measure, and an AI tool that knew nothing about any of it. Every handoff between tools was lossy. Every per-seat license punished growth. Every data enrichment cost money before a single conversation happened. And the reps at the center of it all were spending more time updating records than having the conversations that actually closed revenue.

The insight that changed everything was architectural: what if every signal, contact, conversation, deal, and campaign lived on one shared graph — a single buyer record that every agent, every app, and every rep could read from and write to in real time? Not seven tools pretending to talk to each other. One system where buyer motion starts the work automatically, agents carry the volume, and humans step in only for the live moments that machines cannot replace.

That insight became graph8. Founded in 2024 and backed by $10M in seed funding, graph8 was built not as a feature addition to the existing stack, but as a wholesale replacement of it. The platform combines 15 named AI agents, a 7-app sales engagement suite (Sequencer, Dialer, Inbox, Web Chat, Meetings, Nurture, Newsletter), a native CRM with quote-to-cash automation, a buyer graph of 700M+ verified B2B contacts and 100M+ companies, a built-in Customer Data Platform with 500+ source connectors, real-time intent signals processing approximately 2 billion buying signals per day, AI voice agents, Agent Twins trained on individual rep voices and styles, content generation via Studio, and developer infrastructure via MCP, REST API, and CLI — all on one shared buyer graph.

Today, graph8 serves revenue teams from solo founders to enterprise organizations across Sales, Marketing, RevOps, Leadership, Customer Success, and Developer roles. The platform is priced by execution rather than per-seat licenses — meaning the whole team can use it without the headcount tax that compounds with every hire. The Programmable Revenue Community publishes weekly GTM research every Tuesday, extending the mission beyond software into education and operator development.

The vision ahead is unambiguous: graph8 becomes the definitive autonomous revenue operating system for B2B — the single system where AI agents do the prospecting, outreach, qualification, and follow-up; where a native CRM tracks every deal from signal to cash; where a built-in CDP unifies every data source; where developers can build revenue products on top of the buyer graph via SDK, MCP, REST, and CLI; and where every rep walks into every call as the most prepared person in the room. Revenue is programmable. graph8 is the system you run it on.

**Brand Mission Narrative:** graph8 exists because the way B2B revenue gets built is architecturally broken — not because people aren't working hard enough, but because the tools they work in were never designed to share a single version of the truth. A decade of running real outbound campaigns at scale through CIENCE proved this conclusively. The revenue stack had become a collection of disconnected point tools, each charging per seat, each holding its own slice of buyer context, and none of them capable of acting on the full picture.

graph8's mission is to make revenue programmable. That means building the infrastructure where every buying signal — a visitor hitting your pricing page, a company posting SDR roles, a champion changing jobs, a form submission, a keyword intent spike — is resolved to a real person on a live buyer graph, triggers an autonomous agent to do the work, and routes a fully briefed human to the conversation that matters. It means giving every revenue role — SDR, AE, RevOps, marketer, CSM, CRO, founder, developer — one system where they can see the same truth, act on the same data, and compound every action into a smarter next move.

graph8 serves its customers by doing the work that machines are better at — prospecting, sequencing, enriching, qualifying, drafting, logging, routing — and reserving the live moments for the humans who are better at them. It serves developers by exposing the full buyer graph and revenue primitives via SDK, MCP server, REST API, and CLI, so they can build revenue products without assembling the infrastructure themselves. It serves the broader GTM community through the Programmable Revenue Community and AI-GTM training programs, ensuring that the shift to autonomous revenue is navigable for every operator, not just the technically elite.

The change graph8 seeks to create is a world where revenue is no longer dependent on headcount — where a two-person startup runs the same quality of outbound motion as a hundred-person enterprise team, where a CRO gets a defensible forecast from live data rather than a spreadsheet reconciled the night before the board call, and where every rep walks into every call already knowing the three things that will win the room. graph8 believes programmable revenue is not a future state. It is happening now, and it is what every B2B team deserves.

## Story Frameworks

### The Stack Rebellion

**Name:** The Stack Rebellion
**Description:** A challenger narrative that positions graph8 against the status quo of disconnected point tools. This framework dramatizes the familiar pain of tool sprawl, names the structural cause, and reveals graph8 as the architectural solution the market has been waiting for. It works by validating the audience's frustration before presenting the alternative.
**Structure:**
- Name the broken system: the 8-to-12 tool GTM stack, each tool with its own per-seat tax and its own slice of buyer truth
- Show the human cost: reps spending more time updating records than having conversations, RevOps acting as the integration layer, data that disagrees with itself by Monday morning
- Identify the root cause: it's not the tools individually — it's that they were never designed to share one buyer graph
- Introduce the architectural alternative: one system where every signal, contact, conversation, deal, and campaign reads and writes to the same record
- Demonstrate the outcome: buyer motion starts the work automatically, agents carry the volume, humans step in for the live moment
- Issue the challenge: stop paying the data tax before a single campaign runs

**When To Use:** Most effective for demand generation content targeting RevOps leaders, CROs, and founders who are actively managing tool proliferation. Use in long-form blog posts, conference talks, LinkedIn thought leadership, and competitive displacement campaigns against ZoomInfo, Apollo, Outreach, Salesloft, and Segment.
**Example:** Most revenue teams are running eight tools that were never designed to talk to each other. Apollo holds the contacts. Outreach holds the sequences. The CRM holds the deals. Gong holds the calls. Segment holds the events. Each one charges per seat. None of them shares a buyer graph. So on Monday morning, RevOps reconciles them manually, reps update three systems after every call, and the forecast is already stale before the review starts. graph8 is what happens when you build the whole motion on one graph from the start. Signals resolve to real people automatically. Agents do the prospecting, enriching, sequencing, and follow-up. My Desk tells each rep which three deals need a move today. The CRM fills itself. And the forecast comes from the deals your reps actually work — not a spreadsheet someone built on Sunday night.

### The Decade in the Data

**Name:** The Decade in the Data
**Description:** An origin-authority narrative that uses graph8's CIENCE heritage to establish credibility before making any product claim. This framework positions graph8 not as a new AI startup making bold promises, but as the crystallization of ten years of real outbound data into an autonomous system. The authority is the product.
**Structure:**
- Establish the proving ground: ten years of real B2B outbound campaigns run by CIENCE across 2,500+ brands, including names like Okta, Google, Microsoft, and Salesforce
- Name what was learned at scale: what actually books meetings, what closes deals, what signals predict buyer intent, what makes an outreach motion compound over time
- Explain the problem with current AI: most AI sales tools are trained on synthetic data or generic LLM outputs — they don't know what actually worked in real campaigns
- Reveal the advantage: graph8's agents are grounded in a decade of real campaign outcomes, real reply patterns, real meeting-booking mechanics
- Connect to the product: that's why the SDR Agent books, the Deal Agent moves stages, and the AE Cockpit ranks by urgency — because the playbooks are trained on what worked, not what sounded good
- Close with confidence: this is not a new guess at what works. This is the playbook, running autonomously.

**When To Use:** Most effective when competing against newer AI SDR point tools like Artisan, 11x.ai, or Relevance AI, or when building credibility with enterprise buyers who are skeptical of AI claims. Use in sales presentations, case study narratives, and analyst briefings.
**Example:** Before graph8 wrote a line of product code, it ran ten years of real B2B outbound at scale through CIENCE — booking meetings for 2,500+ companies, running millions of touchpoints, and learning exactly what drives a reply, what moves a deal, and what signals predict a buyer is ready to talk. That decade of real campaign data is the foundation of every agent in graph8. The SDR Agent doesn't guess at what personalization works — it's tuned on what actually booked meetings. The Deal Agent doesn't invent next-step plays — it surfaces the moves that closed deals at scale. Most AI sales platforms are trained on what sounds right. graph8 is trained on what worked.

### The Human Node

**Name:** The Human Node
**Description:** A values-forward narrative that resolves the tension between AI automation and human relationship-building. This framework positions the human rep not as a casualty of automation but as the protagonist empowered by it. It speaks directly to the fear that AI will replace salespeople, and reframes that fear as an opportunity.
**Structure:**
- Acknowledge the tension: AI is doing more and more of the revenue work, and it makes sense to wonder where the human fits
- Name what AI is genuinely better at: volume, speed, consistency — prospecting, enriching, sequencing, logging, drafting at machine scale, 24/7
- Name what humans are genuinely better at: live conversations, trust-building, reading the room, handling the objection that matters, earning the close
- Show the handoff moment: the agent works the account, qualifies the interest, books the meeting, and briefs the rep before the call — so the human walks in as the most prepared person in the room
- Demonstrate the amplification: every rep operates like the best rep on the team, because they walk into every call with the full buying history, the open objection, and the next-step play already surfaced
- Land the thesis: AI runs the volume. You win the room. The deal and the relationship stay yours.

**When To Use:** Most effective for sales audience content (AE, SDR, Account Manager), conference keynotes, and any marketing moment where the audience might be skeptical of AI replacing human sellers. Use in role-specific landing pages, email nurture sequences, and video content.
**Example:** graph8 does not replace the rep on the call. It replaces everything that happens before the call and after the call — the prospecting, the prep, the logging, the follow-up. So when the call actually happens, the rep is the most prepared person in the room. They know who is on the call, what they care about, what the last activity was, what the open objection is, and what the next-step play should be. That's what My Desk delivers every morning. That's what the Deal Agent preps before every meeting. The agent ran the volume. The human wins the moment.

### The Signal-to-Revenue Loop

**Name:** The Signal-to-Revenue Loop
**Description:** A product narrative that walks the audience through the complete end-to-end motion from first buying signal to closed revenue on one buyer graph. This framework demonstrates the breadth of the platform by showing how each product connects to the next in a single unbroken loop.
**Structure:**
- Start with the signal: a visitor hits your pricing page three times, a company posts three SDR roles, a champion changes jobs — all resolved to real people on the buyer graph
- Show the automatic launch: the signal scores for ICP fit and intent, a campaign launches automatically, the SDR Agent begins the sequence across email, LinkedIn, SMS, and phone
- Walk through the conversation: the AI Receptionist handles inbound chat, the Voice AI qualifies calls and books meetings, the Inbox Agent drafts replies in the rep's tone
- Enter the deal motion: My Desk ranks the deal, the Deal Agent preps the brief, the AE walks in fully prepared, Quotes handles CPQ and e-sign, billing provisions on signature
- Close the loop: revenue lands in Forecasting, the CRO Agent reads the same data, the CSM Agent watches the account post-sale for churn risk and expansion signals
- Compound the learning: every outcome feeds back into the buyer graph and revenue memory, making every subsequent signal smarter

**When To Use:** Most effective for product demos, website homepage narratives, investor storytelling, and onboarding content. Shows the full platform value in a single coherent arc that no point tool can match.
**Example:** Northwind visits your pricing page three times. graph8 resolves the anonymous visitor to a real company and a real buying committee. Signals scores the account against your ICP — strong fit, high intent. A campaign launches automatically. The SDR Agent sequences the VP Sales across email and LinkedIn. She replies. The Inbox Agent drafts a response in your rep's voice. A meeting gets booked. Voice AI joins the call, qualifies the interest, and sends the rep a live transcript before they join. My Desk surfaces the deal, ranks it by urgency, and briefs the rep before the call. The AE walks in knowing every stakeholder, every objection, and the next-step play. The deal moves to proposal. Quotes generates the CPQ, sends the e-sign, provisions billing on signature. Revenue lands. The CSM Agent watches the account for churn signals 90 days before the renewal. The whole loop ran on one buyer graph.

### The Programmable Revenue Story

**Name:** The Programmable Revenue Story
**Description:** A visionary, category-creation narrative that positions graph8 as the company defining a new category: programmable revenue. This framework is aspirational and forward-looking, designed to attract early adopters, investors, media, and the GTM community at large.
**Structure:**
- Name the era ending: the era of manual, headcount-dependent, tool-stitched revenue operations
- Name the era beginning: the era of programmable revenue — where buying signals automatically trigger campaigns, agents run the motion, and the system learns from every outcome
- Define what programmable means: revenue as infrastructure, not effort — every motion triggerable by code, every workflow automatable, every outcome logged and compoundable
- Show who benefits first: AI-native teams, founders, developers who build on graph8's MCP and API, and RevOps operators who want one source of truth
- Show who benefits next: the entire B2B market as the standard shifts from seat-based tool stacks to autonomous revenue systems
- Invite the audience in: the Programmable Revenue Community, the AI-GTM training, the free buyer graph access — the on-ramps are open

**When To Use:** Most effective for thought leadership content, conference keynotes, media interviews, analyst relations, and community building. Use the Programmable Revenue Community branding and Tuesday calls as proof that the category is already forming.
**Example:** Revenue used to require headcount. More pipeline meant more SDRs. More territory meant more AEs. More accounts meant more CSMs. That model is ending. The new model is programmable revenue: buying signals automatically resolve to real people, agents launch campaigns, qualify interest, book meetings, and log everything — and your reps step in for the conversations that win the relationship. graph8 is the system you run programmable revenue on. One buyer graph. Fifteen named agents. Seven engagement apps. A native CRM. A built-in CDP. And a pricing model that charges for execution, not seats. Revenue isn't a headcount problem anymore. It's an infrastructure problem. And infrastructure is programmable.

structured_data.brand_origin_story:
The story of graph8 begins inside CIENCE — a company that spent a decade running real B2B outbound campaigns at scale for thousands of companies, including brands like Okta, Google, Microsoft, Uber, Salesforce, and Segment. After running millions of outbound touches and booking meetings across 2,500+ B2B brands, the team arrived at a painful and undeniable insight: the revenue stack was fundamentally broken.

The problem wasn't effort. Revenue teams were working hard. The problem was architecture. Every team was stitching together eight, ten, sometimes twelve disconnected point tools — a data vendor here, a sequencer there, a dialer somewhere else, a CRM that barely talked to any of them, a CDP bolted on for good measure, and an AI tool that knew nothing about any of it. Every handoff between tools was lossy. Every per-seat license punished growth. Every data enrichment cost money before a single conversation happened. And the reps at the center of it all were spending more time updating records than having the conversations that actually closed revenue.

The insight that changed everything was architectural: what if every signal, contact, conversation, deal, and campaign lived on one shared graph — a single buyer record that every agent, every app, and every rep could read from and write to in real time? Not seven tools pretending to talk to each other. One system where buyer motion starts the work automatically, agents carry the volume, and humans step in only for the live moments that machines cannot replace.

That insight became graph8. Founded in 2024 and backed by $10M in seed funding, graph8 was built not as a feature addition to the existing stack, but as a wholesale replacement of it. The platform combines 15 named AI agents, a 7-app sales engagement suite (Sequencer, Dialer, Inbox, Web Chat, Meetings, Nurture, Newsletter), a native CRM with quote-to-cash automation, a buyer graph of 700M+ verified B2B contacts and 100M+ companies, a built-in Customer Data Platform with 500+ source connectors, real-time intent signals processing approximately 2 billion buying signals per day, AI voice agents, Agent Twins trained on individual rep voices and styles, content generation via Studio, and developer infrastructure via MCP, REST API, and CLI — all on one shared buyer graph.

Today, graph8 serves revenue teams from solo founders to enterprise organizations across Sales, Marketing, RevOps, Leadership, Customer Success, and Developer roles. The platform is priced by execution rather than per-seat licenses — meaning the whole team can use it without the headcount tax that compounds with every hire. The Programmable Revenue Community publishes weekly GTM research every Tuesday, extending the mission beyond software into education and operator development.

The vision ahead is unambiguous: graph8 becomes the definitive autonomous revenue operating system for B2B — the single system where AI agents do the prospecting, outreach, qualification, and follow-up; where a native CRM tracks every deal from signal to cash; where a built-in CDP unifies every data source; where developers can build revenue products on top of the buyer graph via SDK, MCP, REST, and CLI; and where every rep walks into every call as the most prepared person in the room. Revenue is programmable. graph8 is the system you run it on.
structured_data.brand_mission_narrative:
graph8 exists because the way B2B revenue gets built is architecturally broken — not because people aren't working hard enough, but because the tools they work in were never designed to share a single version of the truth. A decade of running real outbound campaigns at scale through CIENCE proved this conclusively. The revenue stack had become a collection of disconnected point tools, each charging per seat, each holding its own slice of buyer context, and none of them capable of acting on the full picture.

graph8's mission is to make revenue programmable. That means building the infrastructure where every buying signal — a visitor hitting your pricing page, a company posting SDR roles, a champion changing jobs, a form submission, a keyword intent spike — is resolved to a real person on a live buyer graph, triggers an autonomous agent to do the work, and routes a fully briefed human to the conversation that matters. It means giving every revenue role — SDR, AE, RevOps, marketer, CSM, CRO, founder, developer — one system where they can see the same truth, act on the same data, and compound every action into a smarter next move.

graph8 serves its customers by doing the work that machines are better at — prospecting, sequencing, enriching, qualifying, drafting, logging, routing — and reserving the live moments for the humans who are better at them. It serves developers by exposing the full buyer graph and revenue primitives via SDK, MCP server, REST API, and CLI, so they can build revenue products without assembling the infrastructure themselves. It serves the broader GTM community through the Programmable Revenue Community and AI-GTM training programs, ensuring that the shift to autonomous revenue is navigable for every operator, not just the technically elite.

The change graph8 seeks to create is a world where revenue is no longer dependent on headcount — where a two-person startup runs the same quality of outbound motion as a hundred-person enterprise team, where a CRO gets a defensible forecast from live data rather than a spreadsheet reconciled the night before the board call, and where every rep walks into every call already knowing the three things that will win the room. graph8 believes programmable revenue is not a future state. It is happening now, and it is what every B2B team deserves.

**Competitor:** Cognism
**Comparable Tier:** Data / Contact Enrichment
**Their Price:** ~$1,500/user/year (from graph8's Data Tax Calculator, published 2025 list prices)
**Our Advantage:** graph8 contact search is free; waterfall enrichment is included in the Team Plan with pay-on-match pricing for third-party providers.

### Lusha

**Competitor:** Lusha
**Comparable Tier:** Data / Contact Enrichment
**Their Price:** ~$612/user/year (from graph8's Data Tax Calculator, published 2025 list prices)
**Our Advantage:** graph8 includes unlimited contact data in Team Plan at $99/month flat for unlimited users, with no per-seat or per-record fees.

**Price Positioning:** graph8 positions itself as radically affordable relative to the fragmented stacks it replaces. The core value proposition is 'pay for execution, not seats' — directly attacking the per-seat licensing model of competitors like ZoomInfo ($15,000+/yr), Apollo ($588/user/yr), 6sense ($60,000+/yr), Outreach, Salesloft, and Orum. At $99/month flat for unlimited users with no data vendor required, graph8 markets itself as the tool that eliminates the 'data tax, seat tax, and tool tax' that B2B teams pay before any campaign runs. The Data Tax Calculator on the website illustrates this: a typical stack of ZoomInfo + Apollo + 6sense + Orum + Chili Piper can cost $37,200+/year before execution — vs. graph8 at $99/month ($1,188/year) for equivalent or greater functionality. This is an aggressive value-based positioning aimed at consolidation buyers: SMBs, startups, and mid-market teams who are paying 6-10 vendors and want one bill. Enterprise pricing is custom and not publicly disclosed, maintaining negotiation flexibility at the high end.

## Pricing Objections

### Item 1

**Objection:** We already pay for ZoomInfo/Apollo/6sense — why would we add another tool?
**Response:** graph8 is designed to replace those tools, not add to them. The Team Plan at $99/month includes contact data (700M+), intent signals, visitor ID, sequencer, dialer, AI voice, CRM, and meetings — all on one bill. The Data Tax Calculator at graph8.com/data-tax-calculator lets you compare your current stack cost against graph8 using your own numbers. Most teams find they save $15,000–$50,000+ per year in tool consolidation before counting execution savings.
**Alternative Offer:** Run the Data Tax Calculator at graph8.com/data-tax-calculator with your current stack to see the comparison.

### Item 2

**Objection:** $99/month seems too cheap — what's the catch?
**Response:** The $99/month flat rate covers unlimited users and all features. graph8 makes money on execution credits — what the system does for you (sends, calls, enrichments, bookings, AI generation). The more you run, the more credits you use. But the base platform access, all feature unlocks, unlimited users, and contact data browsing are genuinely included. There's no seat expansion trap.
**Alternative Offer:** Start with the 7-day free trial — no credit card, full platform, no commitment.

### Item 3

**Objection:** We need per-seat pricing for budget allocation across teams.
**Response:** graph8 intentionally does not price per seat, because per-seat pricing penalizes growth and creates adoption friction. The flat $99/month Team Plan is designed to be allocated as one line item covering the whole revenue org. For Finance teams that need seat-level cost attribution, the RevOps reporting layer can provide usage data per user to support internal chargebacks.
**Alternative Offer:** The MCP Unlimited plan at $25/user/month is available if per-user pricing is specifically required for a subset of users.

### Item 4

**Objection:** We have enterprise security and compliance requirements.
**Response:** graph8 is SOC 2 Type II certified, offers GDPR standard contractual clauses, DPA, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning (in pilot), audit logs exportable to SIEM, regional data residency (US, EU, APAC), and full self-hosted deployment for sovereign data requirements. Enterprise pricing is custom — let's schedule a 30-minute discovery call.
**Alternative Offer:** Request the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA through the account executive team.

### Item 5

**Objection:** We're not ready to commit — can we pilot first?
**Response:** Yes. The Team Plan includes a 7-day free trial with no credit card required. For Midmarket teams, a 30-day pilot path is available. Alternatively, the $1,000 Programmable Revenue Blueprint is a fixed-price, three-week diagnostic covering every role in your sales org — a low-risk way to see the system working on your actual ICP before a full commitment.
**Alternative Offer:** $1,000 Programmable Revenue Blueprint or 30-day pilot path for Midmarket.

## Pricing Faqs

### Item 1

**Question:** What does 'execution credits' mean?
**Answer:** Execution credits are consumed when graph8 does real work on your behalf: AI generation, outreach sends (email, SMS, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, phone), voice minutes, meeting bookings, and third-party waterfall enrichment matches. Searching and browsing 700M+ contacts and 100M+ companies never costs a credit on any plan.

### Item 2

**Question:** Are there seat fees?
**Answer:** No. graph8 has unlimited users on all plans. Pricing never scales with headcount. You can invite everyone — sales, marketing, RevOps, founders, agencies — without the bill increasing.

### Item 3

**Question:** What is free, and what costs credits?
**Answer:** Free (always): searching 700M+ contacts, 100M+ companies, 30B+ intent signals, website-visitor identification, and building audiences. Credits are required for: reveals, enrichments, sends, calls (voice minutes), AI generation, meeting bookings, and third-party waterfall provider matches. The first 1,000 contact reveals and 500 execution actions are free on PAYG and developer plans.

### Item 4

**Question:** Is there a free trial?
**Answer:** Yes. The Team Plan includes a 7-day free trial with no credit card required. The Pay as You Go plan starts free with 1,000 contact reveals and 500 execution actions at no cost, no credit card required.

### Item 5

**Question:** Can I cancel anytime?
**Answer:** Yes. All plans are month-to-month with no contracts. Cancel anytime.

### Item 6

**Question:** What is MCP Unlimited and why is it included in the Team Plan?
**Answer:** MCP Unlimited ($25/user/month as a standalone plan) gives unlimited contact data access via the MCP server (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code). On the Team Plan, this is included for every user in the org at no additional cost — described as 'a $25 per user value, included for the whole org on the Team plan.'

### Item 7

**Question:** How does pricing work for the developer API?
**Answer:** Three tiers: PAYG (free to start, then $0.05/credit), Single Org ($25/month, credits drop to $0.01 each), and Developer multi-tenant ($99/month, create and manage orgs per customer). Anything beyond these three shapes is agreed in terms, not published as a list price.

### Item 8

**Question:** Is enterprise pricing available?
**Answer:** Yes, but not publicly listed. Enterprise pricing is custom and includes SSO, SCIM, audit logs, regional data residency, self-hosted deployment, contractual SLAs, and dedicated support. Contact the account executive team to begin an evaluation.

## Negotiation Guidelines

- Enterprise pricing is custom and agreed in contract terms — not published as a list price. Engage account executive team for enterprise evaluation.
- A 30-minute discovery call is the recommended first step for larger teams — no commitment required.
- A 30-day pilot path is available for Midmarket customers.
- The $1,000 Programmable Revenue Blueprint is a fixed-price entry point for teams wanting a structured diagnostic before platform commitment.
- GTM Services (expert operators via Talent Marketplace) are available at zero markup — pricing reflects operator cost only.
- Anything beyond the three published developer plan tiers (PAYG / $25 / $99) is agreed in terms, not on a public price list.
- Waterfall enrichment through third-party providers is pay-on-match; teams can bring their own provider keys to make that provider free — useful negotiating point for data-heavy teams.
- Enterprise self-hosted deployment is available for regulated industries and sovereign data requirements — scope and pricing agreed per contract.

**Max Discount:** Not publicly disclosed

**Approval Matrix:** Not publicly disclosed. Enterprise custom pricing and terms are agreed per contract and require engagement with graph8's account executive team.

meta_data.content:
# Proof Catalog

**Proof Summary:** graph8 is an early-stage B2B SaaS company (founded 2024, $10M Seed) with strong platform-level proof points grounded in its CIENCE heritage — 10 years of real outbound campaign data across 2,500+ B2B brands, millions of conversations, and 30B intent signals. The website prominently displays heritage logos from CIENCE campaigns (Okta, Google, Microsoft, Uber, Salesforce, Segment, Airbnb, BetterHelp, WEX, Instapage, VeChain) with an explicit disclaimer that these are not current graph8 platform customers. No verified case studies or direct customer testimonials for the graph8 platform itself were found on the website. The strongest proof assets are quantitative platform statistics (700M+ contacts, 100M+ companies, 30B signals, 2B signals/day, 500+ connectors, 15 named agents, 150+ MCP tools, 460+ API operations) and structural proof from the underlying CIENCE and Tenbound infrastructure. The proof catalog is weighted toward platform capabilities, heritage credibility, and enterprise-grade certifications (SOC 2 Type II). Priority gaps to close: verified graph8 platform customer case studies, direct testimonials from paying users, and third-party analyst recognition specific to graph8 (not CIENCE).

**Has Verified Case Studies:** False

## Statistics

### Item 1

**Stat:** 700M+ verified B2B contacts
**Context:** Total contacts in graph8's Buyer Graph database, searchable free on every plan across all user seats
**Source:** graph8.com/platform/data
**Methodology:** Platform-stated figure for the proprietary buyer graph data layer

### Item 2

**Stat:** 100M+ companies
**Context:** Total company records in graph8's Buyer Graph, with account intelligence including tech stack and buying committee data
**Source:** graph8.com/platform/data

# Value Props

## Master Value Prop

**Proposition:** graph8 is the autonomous revenue system that unifies AI agents, a 7-app sales engagement suite, native CRM, 700M+ contact buyer graph, and a built-in CDP on one platform — so B2B teams can run every motion from first signal to closed revenue without stitching together eight disconnected tools.
**Headline:** One buyer graph. Every revenue motion. Agents do the work. Reps win the moment.
**Target Segment:** B2B revenue teams — Sales, Marketing, RevOps, Leadership, Customer Success, and Developers — at companies from startups to enterprise who are frustrated by tool sprawl, per-seat pricing, and fragmented data that makes every handoff lossy.
**Primary Benefit:** Replace the entire GTM stack — data vendor, sequencer, dialer, AI SDR, CRM, CDP, and content tool — with one unified platform priced by execution, not headcount, so the whole team operates on the same buyer graph with zero reconciliation.
**Supporting Benefits:**
- Free to search 700M+ contacts and 100M+ companies; pay only when graph8 executes work
- Unlimited users on every paid plan — no seat taxes that punish growth
- 15 named AI agents (SDR Agent, Deal Agent, CSM Agent, Agent Twins, Voice AI, and more) run autonomously 24/7 and hand off to humans at the live sales moment
- Two-way sync with HubSpot, Salesforce, and Pipedrive means you consolidate or coexist — no forced migration
- Built on 10 years of real B2B outbound data from CIENCE — agents are trained on what actually booked meetings and closed deals
- MCP integration gives Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and VS Code live access to the buyer graph with 150+ tools
- Every agent action is logged to revenue memory — auditable, reversible, governed

**Proof Points:**
- 700M+ verified B2B contacts and 100M+ companies available free to search on every plan
- 30B intent signals processed; approximately 2 billion buying signals per day resolved to real people
- 500+ data source connectors in the built-in CDP
- 15 named AI agents covering every revenue role from SDR to CRO
- 7 integrated sales engagement apps sharing one buyer graph
- Backed by $10M seed funding; built on a decade of CIENCE campaign heritage across 2,500+ B2B brands
- Team plan covers unlimited users for $99/month — eliminating the per-seat tax that compounds with every hire

**Differentiator:** graph8 is the only platform that combines 15 named AI agents, a 7-app sales engagement suite, a native CRM, 700M+ verified B2B contacts, a built-in CDP with 500+ connectors, and intent signals — all on a single buyer graph trained on 10 years of real CIENCE campaign data — and prices by execution usage rather than per-seat licenses.

## Value Pillars

### Item 1

**Pillar:** One Buyer Graph — No More Tool Sprawl
**Description:** Every signal, contact, conversation, deal, and campaign lives on a single buyer graph. There is no export, no reconciliation, no integration glue to maintain. Data that lands on the graph from any surface — Sequencer, Dialer, Signals, Agents, CRM, CDP — is instantly available to every other surface, so the next agent and the next rep always see the full picture.
**Claims:**
- Replaces Apollo/ZoomInfo (data), Outreach/Salesloft (sequencing), Orum/Nooks (dialer), Segment/Rudderstack (CDP), Drift/Intercom (chat), Salesforce/HubSpot (CRM), and Jasper/Copy.ai (content) with one platform
- Every app writes back to the same buyer record — no stale exports, no version drift between tools
- Two-way CRM sync with HubSpot, Salesforce, and Pipedrive means existing stacks coexist without data loss
- 500+ CDP connectors ingest every external data source into one unified identity layer
- The Data Tax Calculator shows teams typically save $20K+ per year before a single campaign runs

**Evidence:**
- graph8 ships a native CRM, sequencer, dialer, inbox, chat, meetings, nurture, newsletter, CDP, signals, studio, and AI agents — all on one buyer graph
- Published Data Tax Calculator compares graph8 at $99/month flat against ZoomInfo ($15K/yr), Apollo ($588/user/yr), 6sense ($60K/yr), Orum ($3,600/user/yr), and Chili Piper ($15K/yr) — illustrating $21K+ in annualized savings for a small team
- Unlimited users on the Team plan means adding reps, marketers, and RevOps never increases the platform bill

**Icon:** graph

### Item 2

**Pillar:** AI Agents That Run the Revenue Motion — Humans Win the Moment
**Description:** graph8 deploys 15 named, specialized AI agents that prospect, reply, book, qualify, forecast, draft, and govern — autonomously and around the clock. Agents hand off to humans precisely at the live sales moment, fully briefed, so reps walk into every call as the most prepared person in the room. You set the autonomy lane per agent — Manual, Hybrid, or Autopilot — and change it any time.
**Claims:**
- SDR Agent builds ICP lists, drafts first touches in the rep's voice, handles replies, and books meetings — without a human SDR headcount
- Agent Twins are AI clones of individual reps trained on their deals, writing style, and voice — they leave voicemails, draft replies, and cover reps 24/7
- Voice AI makes and receives calls, qualifies leads, books meetings automatically, and delivers a live transcript to the rep before they join
- Deal Agent preps every call brief with stakeholders, last activity, open objections, next-step play, and talk-track
- CSM Agent monitors every account in the installed base for churn risk 90 days before renewal, then drafts the renewal brief and QBR
- CRO Agent forecasts nightly, flags at-risk deals, surfaces coaching moments, and drafts the operating-cadence agenda
- AI Receptionist handles inbound chat, web forms, email, and phone 24/7 — qualifying leads and booking meetings with zero human involvement until the prospect wants to talk

**Evidence:**
- 15 named agents: SDR Agent, Deal Agent, CSM Agent, CRO Agent, Content Agent, Agent Twins, Voice AI, AI Receptionist, Data Quality Agent, Attribution Agent, Operator Agent, Executor Agent, Research Agent, SEO/AEO Agent, and Control & Safety Agent
- Agent autonomy controls are per-agent and per-channel — founders can put outbound on Autopilot while keeping deal approvals Manual
- Revenue memory logs every agent action with actor, timestamp, and policy reference — making automation auditable and reversible
- All agent actions are visible in My Desk (AE Cockpit) — the ranked daily decision queue that shows meeting prep, interested replies, follow-ups, and at-risk deals with drafted next steps ready for approval

**Icon:** robot

### Item 3

**Pillar:** Verified Buyer Data and Real-Time Intent — Free to Search
**Description:** graph8 ships a live buyer graph of 700M+ verified B2B contacts and 100M+ companies with firmographics, technographics, and conversation history — free to search on every plan. Signals layer on 30B intent records (approximately 2B per day), visitor identification, hiring changes, job changes, and tech stack changes — all resolved to real people and ready to trigger a launch automatically.
**Claims:**

(2) **Human Bottlenecks at Scale**: Manual prospecting, sequencing, and follow-up are linear — more pipeline requires more headcount. Without AI agents running these workflows autonomously, growth is capped by hiring capacity and human bandwidth. (3) **Data Decay and Blind Spots**: Static databases, disconnected identity graphs, and missing enrichment mean reps are working with incomplete or stale buyer intelligence — wasting effort on the wrong contacts and missing buying signals entirely. With graph8, companies replace this status quo with a single AI-native platform where agents run the revenue motion continuously, data stays clean and unified, and every team member works from a live, enriched Buyer Graph — compounding results over time instead of just maintaining the status quo.

structured_data.vs_status_quo: Doing nothing — or continuing to patch together a fragmented stack — means revenue teams keep losing to three silent killers: (1) **Tool Sprawl Tax**: The average B2B revenue team runs 10–15 disconnected tools (CRM, sequencer, dialer, data provider, CDP, chat, collaboration), each with its own contract, admin burden, and data silo. The integration overhead alone consumes RevOps bandwidth that should be focused on growth. (2) **Human Bottlenecks at Scale**: Manual prospecting, sequencing, and follow-up are linear — more pipeline requires more headcount. Without AI agents running these workflows autonomously, growth is capped by hiring capacity and human bandwidth. (3) **Data Decay and Blind Spots**: Static databases, disconnected identity graphs, and missing enrichment mean reps are working with incomplete or stale buyer intelligence — wasting effort on the wrong contacts and missing buying signals entirely. With graph8, companies replace this status quo with a single AI-native platform where agents run the revenue motion continuously, data stays clean and unified, and every team member works from a live, enriched Buyer Graph — compounding results over time instead of just maintaining the status quo.
structured_data.vs_alternatives: **vs. Salesforce + Outreach + ZoomInfo + Segment (Best-of-Breed Stack):** The traditional enterprise stack requires 4–6 figure annual contracts per tool, complex integrations that break with every update, duplicate data across systems, and a full-time RevOps team just to keep it running. graph8 consolidates all of this — CRM (no per-seat fees), sales engagement (7 apps), B2B data (700M+ contacts, free search), CDP (500+ connectors), and AI agents — into one governed platform at a fraction of the total cost of ownership. **vs. HubSpot (All-in-One Mid-Market):** HubSpot unifies marketing and CRM but lacks true AI agent autonomy, native CDP infrastructure, parallel dialing, a live Buyer Graph, and the depth of sales engagement tooling graph8 provides. HubSpot scales poorly for outbound-heavy or complex revenue motions. graph8 is built for the full revenue team — not just marketing. **vs. Clay + Apollo + Instantly (Modern Outbound Stack):** This stack is powerful for data enrichment and sequencing but remains a collection of disconnected tools without a native CRM, CDP, CSM layer, or AI agents that operate across the full revenue motion. graph8 provides everything these tools do — plus the infrastructure layer, collaboration, and post-sale motion in a single platform. **vs. Building In-House:** Assembling a custom AI revenue stack requires significant engineering investment, ongoing maintenance, and model fine-tuning. graph8 delivers 15 pre-built revenue agents, a native Buyer Graph, and a production-ready CDP out of the box — compressing time-to-value from months to days. **vs. Point AI Tools (e.g., standalone AI SDR vendors):** Single-purpose AI SDR tools lack the data layer (Buyer Graph), the downstream workflow (CRM, Quotes, CSM), and the infrastructure (CDP) to close the loop on revenue. graph8's agents are native to the platform — they act on live data, update the CRM, trigger sequences, and hand off to human reps seamlessly without leaving the system.

# Icp Research

**Icp Summary:** graph8's ideal customers are B2B organizations that run structured revenue motions and are actively feeling the pain of operating a fragmented GTM stack — paying per-seat taxes to data vendors, sequencers, dialers, and CRMs that don't share a common data layer. The platform serves four distinct buyer archetypes across company size: (1) B2B SaaS and technology companies at the growth stage (Series A–C or $5M–$100M ARR) with 10–200 person sales and marketing teams who need to scale pipeline without headcount; (2) mid-market revenue organizations (100–1,000 employees) consolidating 6–10 point tools onto one operating system; (3) AI-native startups and developer teams who want to build GTM on API/SDK/MCP primitives rather than buy another SaaS seat; and (4) GTM and lead-gen agencies running outbound for multiple clients who need per-client isolation with shared infrastructure. All four archetypes share a core need: a single buyer graph where signals, contacts, campaigns, conversations, and pipeline live together — and autonomous agents that carry the volume so human reps can focus on the live sales moment. graph8's execution-based pricing (not per-seat) is itself a qualification signal: buyers who are tired of headcount-linked SaaS invoices and want to pay for outcomes are the strongest fits.

## Firmographics

### Company Size (Employees) — Tier 1: Growth-Stage B2B SaaS

**Attribute:** Company Size (Employees) — Tier 1: Growth-Stage B2B SaaS
**Ideal Range:** 10–200 employees
**Acceptable Range:** 5–500 employees
**Disqualifying:** Fewer than 3 employees with no dedicated GTM function; pure B2C with no outbound motion
**Weight:** High

### Company Size (Employees) — Tier 2: Mid-Market Revenue Org

**Attribute:** Company Size (Employees) — Tier 2: Mid-Market Revenue Org
**Ideal Range:** 200–1,000 employees
**Acceptable Range:** 100–2,500 employees
**Disqualifying:** No structured sales team; single-rep shop with no intent to scale
**Weight:** High

### Annual Revenue

**Attribute:** Annual Revenue
**Ideal Range:** $1M–$50M ARR (SaaS); $5M–$500M (Services/Industrial)
**Acceptable Range:** $500K–$200M
**Disqualifying:** Pre-revenue with no GTM budget; Fortune 50 with locked multi-year enterprise procurement (unless via enterprise motion)
**Weight:** Medium

### Funding Stage

**Attribute:** Funding Stage
**Ideal Range:** Seed through Series C; bootstrapped with >$2M ARR
**Acceptable Range:** Series D+; PE-backed mid-market with RevOps mandate
**Disqualifying:** No external funding and <$500K ARR with no near-term hiring plans
**Weight:** Medium

### Sales Team Structure

**Attribute:** Sales Team Structure
**Ideal Range:** Has at least one SDR or AE; VP/Director of Sales or CRO in seat
**Acceptable Range:** Founder-led sales transitioning to first sales hire; agencies with SDR-as-a-service motion
**Disqualifying:** Purely inbound/PLG with no outbound or sales development function
**Weight:** High

### GTM Stack Complexity

**Attribute:** GTM Stack Complexity
**Ideal Range:** Currently paying 3+ separate vendors for data, sequencer, CRM, and/or dialer
**Acceptable Range:** 1–2 point tools but actively evaluating consolidation
**Disqualifying:** Happy with current single-vendor stack with no consolidation intent; entirely manual with no tech appetite
**Weight:** High

### Tech Maturity / AI Readiness

**Attribute:** Tech Maturity / AI Readiness
**Ideal Range:** Team actively uses Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor; has a RevOps or GTM engineering function
**Acceptable Range:** Early AI experimenters; leadership open to AI-native workflows
**Disqualifying:** Explicitly anti-AI culture; procurement requires vendor with >5 years in market
**Weight:** Medium

## Target Industries

- B2B SaaS and Software
- Fintech and Financial Services
- Healthtech and Digital Health
- GTM and Lead Generation Agencies
- Professional Services (Consulting, IT Services, Managed Services)
- Cybersecurity
- Sales Development / SDR Outsourcing
- Developer Tools and API-First Companies
- Marketing Technology
- Revenue Operations Consulting
- AI-Native Startups
- B2B E-commerce and Marketplaces

## Excluded Industries

- Pure B2C Retail and Consumer Goods
- Government and Public Sector (low AI adoption, procurement barriers)
- Non-profit organizations with no sales motion
- Pure inbound-only media and publishing companies
- Regulated industries with no outbound tolerance (e.g., certain healthcare providers subject to strict HIPAA constraints on outbound)
- Companies selling exclusively through channel partners with no direct sales

## Target Geographies

- United States (primary — all regions, with emphasis on major SaaS hubs: SF Bay Area, NYC, Austin, Boston, Seattle, Chicago)
- Canada (secondary — Toronto, Vancouver)
- United Kingdom (secondary — London SaaS and fintech corridor)
- Western Europe (secondary — Germany, Netherlands, France, Nordics)
- Australia and New Zealand (secondary)
- Israel (secondary — strong SaaS and cybersecurity ecosystem)
- Singapore and APAC SaaS hubs (emerging)

**Geo Considerations:** Primary revenue focus is North America (US and Canada) where graph8's CIENCE campaign heritage and Tenbound research are most recognized. EMEA is a strong secondary market, particularly UK and Western Europe, where Cognism competes heavily on data compliance — graph8's SOC 2 Type II and GDPR posture provide a credible entry. APAC is early-stage but viable for AI-native and developer-focused buyers. Self-hosted and regional data residency options (EU, APAC) remove the most common geographic procurement blocker for enterprise buyers outside the US.

**Indicator:** Company posts new SDR, BDR, AE, or RevOps job listings — signals active GTM scaling and budget for outbound tools
**Strength:** Strong

**Indicator:** New CRM adoption is a buying trigger for complementary tools: sequencer, data enrichment, dialer, and intent signals

**Indicator:** Apollo, ZoomInfo, or Cognism contract renewal conversations are a natural switch trigger; monitor for LinkedIn posts complaining about per-seat pricing

**Indicator:** Multi-page, multi-session visitors researching the full platform (not just one product) are evaluating graph8 holistically — high purchase intent

**Indicator:** Conference attendance signals active investment in GTM capability building and peer benchmarking — receptive to graph8 outreach in context

## Qualification Criteria

### Item 1

**Criterion:** Active outbound or sales development motion
**Must Have:** True
**How To Verify:** Check LinkedIn for SDR/BDR/AE job postings; review their website for 'book a demo' or contact forms; ask directly on discovery call how pipeline is currently created
**Questions To Ask:**
- How does your team currently generate outbound pipeline — what does that motion look like week to week?
- Do you have SDRs or AEs running sequences today, and which tools are they using?
- What percentage of your new pipeline comes from outbound vs. inbound?


### Item 2

**Criterion:** Pain with current GTM stack fragmentation — paying multiple vendors for overlapping functions
**Must Have:** True
**How To Verify:** Run the Data Tax Calculator conversation: ask them to list their current vendors for data, sequencer, dialer, CRM. If they list 3+ separate vendors, the consolidation pain is real. Check job postings for RevOps roles — a RevOps hire is a strong signal of stack complexity pain.
**Questions To Ask:**
- How many separate tools does your sales team log into daily to run outreach?
- What does your current annual spend look like across data, sequencer, dialer, and CRM tools combined?
- Where do your biggest data sync or handoff gaps exist between tools today?


### Item 3

**Criterion:** Budget authority or influencer in seat — VP Sales, CRO, Head of RevOps, or Founder
**Must Have:** True
**How To Verify:** Confirm on discovery call who owns the tool consolidation or AI adoption budget; check LinkedIn for title seniority; look for recent leadership hires (new VP Sales or CRO is a strong trigger)
**Questions To Ask:**
- Who on your team would be most involved in evaluating and approving a platform like this?
- Do you own the budget for sales tools, or does that run through RevOps or IT?
- Is there a specific initiative or project driving this evaluation right now?


### Item 4

**Criterion:** Openness to AI-native workflows and agent-assisted execution
**Must Have:** True
**How To Verify:** Ask about current AI tool usage; look for 'AI SDR,' 'AI sales,' or 'automation' in their job descriptions; check if leadership speaks publicly about AI adoption (LinkedIn posts, conference talks)
**Questions To Ask:**
- Is your team currently experimenting with any AI tools for sales or marketing — Claude, ChatGPT, AI SDR platforms?
- How does your leadership feel about autonomous agents handling outreach and qualification?
- What level of human approval would you want on outbound actions before they go out?


### Item 5

**Criterion:** B2B business model with a defined ICP and sales cycle
**Must Have:** True
**How To Verify:** Confirm they sell to other businesses (not purely B2C); verify they have a defined target customer segment and a repeatable sales motion (not purely transactional/marketplace)
**Questions To Ask:**
- Walk me through your typical customer — who are you selling to, what's the title, what's the company size?
- What does a typical sales cycle look like for you — days, weeks, or months?
- Do you have a defined ICP and buyer persona, or is that still being figured out?


### Item 6

**Criterion:** Technical receptiveness to API/MCP/SDK integration (for developer and builder segments)
**Must Have:** False
**How To Verify:** Check if company has a RevOps engineer, GTM engineer, or developer in the GTM function; look for technical job postings; ask about current API usage or automation scripts
**Questions To Ask:**
- Do you have anyone on the GTM team who can work with APIs or write lightweight automation scripts?
- Have you connected Claude, Cursor, or ChatGPT to any of your business data or tools yet?
- Are you building any internal revenue tooling or apps on top of your current stack?


## Disqualifiers

### Item 1

**Criterion:** Purely B2C business with no account-based or enterprise sales motion
**Reason:** graph8's entire platform is built for B2B buyer graphs — contact records, firmographic targeting, buying committees, and account-level intent signals. B2C companies have no use for 700M verified B2B contacts, SDR agents, or AE cockpits.
**Exceptions:** B2C companies with a B2B partnerships, enterprise, or agency sales arm can still qualify for those specific revenue motions

### Item 2

**Criterion:** No outbound or sales development function and explicit refusal to build one
**Reason:** graph8's core value — autonomous agents running prospecting, sequencing, dialing, and booking — requires a company to have (or want to build) an outbound motion. Purely inbound PLG companies with no sales team have limited use for the platform's most differentiated capabilities.
**Exceptions:** Purely inbound companies can still use graph8's Signals, Buyer Graph data, Studio, AI Receptionist, and CDP — but LTV is significantly lower

### Item 3

**Criterion:** Under 3 employees with no GTM budget and no near-term hiring plan
**Reason:** The platform requires at minimum one person responsible for revenue to see meaningful ROI. Solo founders with zero budget should start on the free tier but are not enterprise pipeline candidates.
**Exceptions:** Solo founders and solopreneurs are a valid free-tier and MCP Unlimited segment — do not disqualify from self-serve; only deprioritize for sales-assisted pipeline

### Item 4

**Criterion:** Requires on-premise-only deployment in a region or sector where graph8's self-hosted option is not yet available
**Reason:** Enterprise buyers in highly regulated sectors (e.g., defense, some government, certain financial institutions) may require infrastructure certifications or deployment models graph8 does not currently offer at scale.
**Exceptions:** graph8 offers self-hosted deployment for enterprise — engage the enterprise team before disqualifying; SOC 2 Type II, GDPR DPA, and regional residency cover most regulated buyers

### Item 5

**Criterion:** Procurement cycle exceeding 12 months with no executive sponsor or budget pre-allocated
**Reason:** graph8 is month-to-month with no annual lock-in, and is priced by execution — not by enterprise seat negotiation. Buyers whose procurement process requires a 12+ month vendor assessment without budget pre-approval represent a poor resource allocation for sales cycles.
**Exceptions:** Large enterprise deals with a named executive sponsor and pre-allocated budget are worth pursuing even with longer timelines

### Item 6

**Criterion:** Cultural or executive-level rejection of AI-assisted sales and outbound automation
**Reason:** graph8's differentiated value is autonomous AI agents running the revenue motion. Buyers who philosophically oppose AI-generated outreach, AI voice calls, or agent-assisted workflows will reject the platform's core value proposition and create churn risk.
**Exceptions:** Companies that want 'manual mode only' (agents propose, human approves everything) can still work within graph8's approval-gate framework — probe the specific objection before disqualifying

### Item 7

**Criterion:** No existing or planned CRM usage and no data management discipline
**Reason:** graph8's buyer graph and revenue memory require at minimum a willingness to track contacts and deals. Companies with zero data hygiene practices and no intent to build them cannot leverage the platform's unified data layer and will have poor activation outcomes.

## Icp Tiers

### Tier 1 — Best Fit: Growth-Stage B2B SaaS / Tech (Series A–C)

**Tier Name:** Tier 1 — Best Fit: Growth-Stage B2B SaaS / Tech (Series A–C)
**Description:** B2B SaaS companies between 10–200 employees running structured outbound with a fractured stack. They have at least one SDR or AE, a VP Sales or CRO in seat, and are paying 3–6 separate vendors for data, sequencing, dialing, and CRM. They feel the per-seat tax acutely as the team scales. Leadership is AI-curious and the company has adopted Claude, ChatGPT, or similar tools informally. They want to consolidate onto one system with an execution-based pricing model so costs scale with outcomes, not headcount.
**Criteria:**
- 10–200 employees
- Series A, B, or C funded (or bootstrapped with >$2M ARR)
- Active outbound motion with SDR or AE team
- Currently using Apollo/ZoomInfo + Outreach/Salesloft + HubSpot/Salesforce across separate contracts
- VP Sales, CRO, or Head of RevOps as economic buyer
- AI-open culture — team using Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor informally
- B2B SaaS, fintech, healthtech, dev tools, or cybersecurity vertical

**Expected Ltv:** $2,400–$24,000+ ARR (Team plan to custom enterprise); highest LTV when they adopt the full platform including Agents, CRM, Data, and Studio
**Sales Approach:** Lead with the Data Tax Calculator and stack consolidation narrative. Show the exact annual tax they pay across ZoomInfo + Outreach + Orum + HubSpot before a single campaign runs, then contrast with graph8's $99/month Team plan for unlimited users. Run a live demo on the Buyer Graph (free search) and Signals to show immediate time-to-value. Reference the CIENCE heritage for credibility with outbound-savvy buyers. Propose a 7-day free trial with the full platform.

### Tier 2 — Strong Fit: Mid-Market Revenue Organization (100–1,000 Employees)

**Tier Name:** Tier 2 — Strong Fit: Mid-Market Revenue Organization (100–1,000 Employees)
**Description:** Structured revenue organizations with 25–100+ sales reps across multiple territories or product lines. They have a formal RevOps function, a VP Sales and CRO, and are managing the complexity of per-territory pipelines, rep ramp, and forecast reliability. Their stack is sprawling — Salesforce or HubSpot as the CRM of record, Outreach or Salesloft for sequencing, ZoomInfo or Cognism for data, Orum or Aircall for dialing, and often Clay or a custom RevOps build for enrichment. They need one source of truth and agents that keep coverage complete as the team scales.
**Criteria:**
- 100–1,000 employees with 25+ quota-carrying reps
- Formal RevOps function or dedicated RevOps hire
- Multi-territory or multi-product sales motion
- Salesforce or HubSpot as CRM of record
- Active contract with 4+ separate GTM vendors
- CRO or VP Sales sponsoring a stack consolidation or AI initiative
- SOC 2 awareness or compliance requirement

**Expected Ltv:** $12,000–$100,000+ ARR; upsell path through enterprise Agents, Voice AI, and GTM Services
**Sales Approach:** Lead with the governance and forecasting narrative — 'one forecast everyone trusts, off live pipeline.' Emphasize the CRO Agent's ability to run the operating cadence nightly, flag at-risk deals 90 days out, and draft the QBR. Show how graph8's native CRM with per-territory pipelines, live leaderboard, and weighted forecast replaces the spreadsheet reconciliation. Highlight two-way CRM sync so they keep Salesforce/HubSpot as a system of record while running all execution on graph8. Offer a 30-day pilot with a named CSM and migration support.

### Tier 3 — Strong Fit: AI-Native Startups and Developer / Builder Teams

**Tier Name:** Tier 3 — Strong Fit: AI-Native Startups and Developer / Builder Teams
**Description:** Teams building revenue software on top of AI (LLM apps, AI agents, no-code tools) or GTM-engineering-forward companies that want to build their GTM the way they build their product — in code. They use Claude, Cursor, or ChatGPT daily and want a buyer graph they can query from their IDE rather than a SaaS dashboard. They value the MCP server, REST API, SDK, and CLI interfaces over UI-first products. They have a strong aversion to per-seat pricing and are drawn to graph8's usage-based execution model.
**Criteria:**
- 5–100 employees; developer or technical co-founder in GTM role
- Active users of Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, or Windsurf for coding and research
- B2B product with a defined ICP and outbound or product-led sales motion
- Preference for API-first, SDK-first, or MCP-first tooling over SaaS dashboards
- Seed to Series B funded or bootstrapped AI-native
- Technical buyer: GTM engineer, developer, or technical founder as champion

**Expected Ltv:** $300–$3,600/year on MCP Unlimited; $1,200–$12,000/year on Team plan; highest value when they build revenue applications on graph8 primitives and become a platform customer
**Sales Approach:** Lead with the developer page (graph8.com/build) and the MCP server narrative — 'give Claude live B2B data.' Show how 700M contacts, 150+ MCP tools, and 150+ REST endpoints give their AI agents real buyers to work with. Demonstrate the SDK quickstart (npm install @graph8/sdk) and the CLI. Emphasize free search with no credit card and unlimited data at $25/user — they pay only when graph8 executes. Community-led: point them to the Programmable Revenue Builder Edition magazine and the Tuesday community call.

### Tier 4 — Strong Fit: GTM and Lead Generation Agencies

**Tier Name:** Tier 4 — Strong Fit: GTM and Lead Generation Agencies
**Description:** Agencies running outbound, demand generation, or SDR-as-a-service for multiple B2B clients. They need per-client isolation (separate buyer graphs, sequencer inboxes, and reporting), the ability to stand up a fresh ICP and brand voice per client from a URL (Studio), and agents that carry the volume so headcount does not cap client count. graph8's Agency Keys, cross-org targeting, and zero-markup Talent Marketplace make it a direct replacement for the multi-vendor agency stack.
**Criteria:**
- Agency or outsourced SDR firm with 2+ active B2B clients on outbound programs
- Manages outbound sequencing, dialing, and/or appointment setting as a core service
- Currently stitching Apollo/ZoomInfo + Instantly/Outreach + Aircall across client accounts
- Ops lead or agency owner as economic buyer
- Per-client reporting and governance requirements
- Interest in the Talent Marketplace (hiring vetted GTM operators or getting hired)

**Expected Ltv:** $2,400–$36,000+ ARR depending on client count and execution volume; strong expansion potential as agency grows client roster
**Sales Approach:** Lead with Agency Keys and per-client buyer graph isolation — 'one platform, every client brand, zero tool sprawl.' Show Studio standing up a fresh ICP, messaging house, and landing page for a new client from a single URL in under 10 minutes. Highlight the Talent Marketplace as a way to staff engagements with vetted operators at zero markup. Reference the CIENCE heritage — graph8 is literally the platform that ran those campaigns. Offer a pilot with one client program, then expand.

**Scoring Model:** Lead scoring is built on four dimensions, each contributing to a 0–100 composite score. Firmographic Fit (30 points): company size 10–1,000 employees in a B2B vertical (+20), active sales team with VP+ buyer (+10). Behavioral Intent (30 points): visited pricing/calculator pages (+15), multiple platform page sessions (+10), signed up for community or free tier (+5). Stack Signal (25 points): pays 3+ separate GTM vendors (+15), using HubSpot or Salesforce (+5), current Apollo/ZoomInfo/Outreach contract detected (+5). Role Signal (15 points): new VP Sales or CRO hire in last 90 days (+10), active SDR/RevOps hiring (+5). Minimum score to route to sales-assisted pipeline: 55/100. Score 70+ triggers immediate SDR Agent outreach sequence. Score 40–54 enters long-cycle nurture via Studio Newsletter and Programmable Revenue Community.

**Minimum Score:** 55/100 composite score across Firmographic Fit, Behavioral Intent, Stack Signal, and Role Signal dimensions

structured_data.icp_summary: graph8's ideal customers are B2B organizations that run structured revenue motions and are actively feeling the pain of operating a fragmented GTM stack — paying per-seat taxes to data vendors, sequencers, dialers, and CRMs that don't share a common data layer. The platform serves four distinct buyer archetypes across company size: (1) B2B SaaS and technology companies at the growth stage (Series A–C or $5M–$100M ARR) with 10–200 person sales and marketing teams who need to scale pipeline without headcount; (2) mid-market revenue organizations (100–1,000 employees) consolidating 6–10 point tools onto one operating system; (3) AI-native startups and developer teams who want to build GTM on API/SDK/MCP primitives rather than buy another SaaS seat; and (4) GTM and lead-gen agencies running outbound for multiple clients who need per-client isolation with shared infrastructure. All four archetypes share a core need: a single buyer graph where signals, contacts, campaigns, conversations, and pipeline live together — and autonomous agents that carry the volume so human reps can focus on the live sales moment. graph8's execution-based pricing (not per-seat) is itself a qualification signal: buyers who are tired of headcount-linked SaaS invoices and want to pay for outcomes are the strongest fits.

# Pains And Gains

**Value Summary:** graph8 eliminates the fragmented, expensive, multi-vendor GTM stack that forces B2B revenue teams to manually stitch together data vendors, sequencers, dialers, CRMs, intent platforms, and content tools — each with its own per-seat tax. By unifying 15 AI agents, a 7-app sales engagement suite, a native CRM, 700M+ B2B contacts, a built-in CDP, and content generation on a single buyer graph, graph8 makes revenue programmable: signals trigger autonomous outreach, the CRM logs itself, and reps walk into every call fully briefed. Teams pay for execution — not seats — and replace five to twelve point tools with one system that runs the full motion from first signal to closed revenue.

## Pain Points

### Fragmented GTM stack: 6–12 disconnected tools each charging per-seat and per-record fees

**Pain:** Fragmented GTM stack: 6–12 disconnected tools each charging per-seat and per-record fees
**Category:** Financial
**Severity:** Critical
**Frequency:** Every billing cycle and every new hire triggers additional cost
**Current Workaround:** Teams manually export CSVs between tools, use Zapier or n8n to stitch integrations, and accept stale or conflicting data across systems
**Cost Of Inaction:** Annual data tax alone can exceed $37,200 for a mid-size team before any campaign executes — and compounds with each new seat or data vendor added
**Affected Personas:**
- CRO
- RevOps
- VP Sales
- Founder/CEO
- Marketing Ops

**Trigger Events:**
- New sales hire added to the stack
- Annual software renewal season
- CFO reviews SaaS spend
- RevOps tasked with stack consolidation
- Data vendor price increase

**Our Solution:** graph8 consolidates CRM, data (700M+ contacts), sequencer, dialer, inbox, meetings, nurture, CDP, signals, studio, and AI agents onto one buyer graph with one bill, unlimited users, and execution-based pricing instead of per-seat fees

### Reps spend the majority of their time on CRM updates, research, and admin instead of selling

**Pain:** Reps spend the majority of their time on CRM updates, research, and admin instead of selling
**Category:** Operational
**Severity:** Critical
**Frequency:** Daily — estimates suggest reps spend 60–70% of their time on non-selling activities
**Current Workaround:** Manual CRM logging after calls, copy-pasting notes, using personal spreadsheets to track follow-ups, and sending generic follow-up emails
**Cost Of Inaction:** Deals stall, pipeline coverage drops, and quota attainment suffers when reps are buried in data entry and manual follow-up instead of live conversations
**Affected Personas:**
- Account Executive
- SDR/BDR
- Sales Manager
- VP Sales

**Trigger Events:**
- Sales QBR reveals reps spending more time on admin than calls
- Pipeline review shows stalled deals with no recent activity logged
- New CRO joins and audits rep productivity
- Rep attrition tied to administrative burden

**Our Solution:** graph8's CRM fills itself — every call, email, and meeting auto-logs. The AE Cockpit ranks the day's priorities by urgency and deal value. Agent Twins draft follow-ups in the rep's voice. The Deal Agent preps each call brief before the rep opens it.

### Missing in-market buyers because buying signals are scattered, delayed, or not monitored

**Pain:** Missing in-market buyers because buying signals are scattered, delayed, or not monitored
**Category:** Strategic
**Severity:** Critical
**Frequency:** Continuously — buying windows are short and teams react days or weeks late
**Current Workaround:** Manually checking LinkedIn for job changes, subscribing to intent data from a separate vendor (6sense, Bombora), running weekly list pulls that are stale before they are used
**Cost Of Inaction:** Competitors who catch intent signals first own the conversation; late outreach reaches buyers who have already shortlisted alternatives
**Affected Personas:**
- SDR/BDR
- Demand Gen Marketer
- VP Sales
- CRO
- RevOps

**Trigger Events:**
- Lost deal post-mortem reveals competitor reached buyer first
- Champion leaves an account and deal goes cold undetected
- Marketing runs campaigns to accounts already past their buying window
- SDR team cannot explain why outreach timing is off

**Our Solution:** graph8 Signals processes ~2 billion buying signals per day — website visitors, intent topics, hiring changes, job changes, tech stack changes — resolves each to a real person on the buyer graph, and automatically launches outreach. Intent and visitor identification are included free.

### Inaccurate, stale, or untrustworthy revenue forecasts that require manual reconciliation

**Pain:** Inaccurate, stale, or untrustworthy revenue forecasts that require manual reconciliation
**Category:** Strategic
**Severity:** High
**Frequency:** Weekly forecast calls and monthly/quarterly board preparation
**Current Workaround:** Weekly spreadsheet roll-ups, Monday morning reconciliation calls between Sales and Finance, parallel forecast models in Clari or separate tools
**Cost Of Inaction:** Missed targets, lost board confidence, misallocated headcount, and bad hiring or investment decisions based on a number nobody trusts
**Affected Personas:**
- CRO
- VP Sales
- RevOps
- Finance/CFO
- Sales Manager

**Trigger Events:**
- Missed quarter blamed on forecast inaccuracy
- CFO challenges CRO forecast in board meeting
- RevOps spending 2+ days per month reconciling pipeline
- New CRO inherits a spreadsheet-based forecasting process

**Our Solution:** graph8's native CRM Forecasting module reads live deal data — weighted by stage and probability — and updates the moment a deal moves. The CRO Agent forecasts nightly, flags at-risk deals 90 days out, and drafts the QBR agenda. One number that Sales, RevOps, and Finance all read from the same source.

**Pain:** Content and campaign creation is slow, inconsistent, and disconnected from actual buyer data
**Category:** Operational
**Severity:** High
**Frequency:** Every campaign launch cycle — typically weeks of production time
**Current Workaround:** Using separate writing tools (Jasper, Copy.ai), briefing freelancers or agencies, manually researching ICP profiles, and launching campaigns without real buyer data grounding

- Content Marketer
- Product Marketer
- Campaign Manager
- Founder/CEO

meta_data.content:
# Persona Research

**Personas Overview:** graph8's buying committee spans six distinct role clusters, each engaging the platform from a different vantage point but all converging on the same core problem: too many disconnected tools, too much manual work, and a revenue motion that stalls the moment a human isn't actively pushing it. The primary buyers are revenue operations leaders and CROs who hold budget and sign contracts; they evaluate graph8as a full-stack replacement for a fragmented point-tool environment. The champions who drive internal momentum are typically VP-level sales leaders or head-of-growth profiles who feel the day-to-day friction most acutely. Secondary influencers include demand generation and marketing managers who need signal-to-pipeline workflows, customer success leaders who want churn visibility, and developers or GTM engineers who evaluate the API and MCP integration surface. Purchase decisions are rarely unilateral — a typical buying committee includes a RevOps or Operations lead as the technical validator, a sales or revenue leader as the economic champion, a CRO or founder as the budget authority, and occasionally a developer or IT representative for security and integration review. graph8's usage-based, unlimited-seat pricing model lowers the adoption barrier significantly and often allows champions to start free and prove value before formal procurement begins. This bottom-up motion means the champion persona is especially important to engage early, as they frequently become the internal sponsor who closes the loop with the decision maker. Anti-personas include B2C businesses, companies with fewer than 10 employees who lack a defined revenue motion, and organizations seeking only a point solution (e.g., a standalone dialer or a single enrichment API) with no interest in consolidating their GTM stack.

## Primary Personas

### RevOps Rachel

**Name:** RevOps Rachel
**Role:** VP of Revenue Operations
**Persona Type:** Decision Maker
**Seniority:** VP/Director
**Department:** Revenue Operations
**Reports To:** CRO or CEO
**Team Size:** 3-8 people
**Experience:** 8-14 years in B2B SaaS, with 3-6 years in RevOps specifically
**Goals:**
- Collapse the fragmented GTM stack into one system of record so data never disagrees with itself across tools
- Give the CRO a forecast she can defend without a Monday-morning spreadsheet reconciliation
- Own the field map, pipeline stage logic, and reporting layer without filing an engineering ticket for every change
- Enable the entire revenue team — sales, marketing, CS — to work from one buyer graph so attribution is a byproduct of unification, not a manual model
- Implement quote-to-cash automation that closes the seam where revenue leaks between CRM rows and billing records
- Reduce the annual 'data tax' (per-seat enrichment, intent vendors, routing tools) that consumes budget before a single campaign runs

**Pain Points:**
- Manages 8-12 disconnected point tools (CRM, sequencer, dialer, enrichment, intent, routing, content, billing) that each require separate logins, contracts, and reconciliation cycles

- Deal-to-cash automation — quote, e-sign, billing provisioning, and commission logging in one auditable flow
- Agent governance — can he set which agent actions require human approval vs. run autonomously, per surface and per region?

The primary buyers are revenue operations leaders and CROs who hold budget and sign contracts; they evaluate graph8as a full-stack replacement for a fragmented point-tool environment. The champions who drive internal momentum are typically VP-level sales leaders or head-of-growth profiles who feel the day-to-day friction most acutely. Secondary influencers include demand generation and marketing managers who need signal-to-pipeline workflows, customer success leaders who want churn visibility, and developers or GTM engineers who evaluate the API and MCP integration surface. Purchase decisions are rarely unilateral — a typical buying committee includes a RevOps or Operations lead as the technical validator, a sales or revenue leader as the economic champion, a CRO or founder as the budget authority, and occasionally a developer or IT representative for security and integration review. graph8's usage-based, unlimited-seat pricing model lowers the adoption barrier significantly and often allows champions to start free and prove value before formal procurement begins.
