# Brand Brief

**Company Name:** graph8

**Industry:** B2B SaaS

**Founded:** 2024

**Mission:** To make revenue programmable by unifying AI agents, sales engagement, CRM, buyer data, intent signals, content generation, data infrastructure, and GTM services on a single buyer graph — so every B2B team can run their entire revenue motion autonomously from first signal to closed revenue.

**Vision:** By 2029, graph8 becomes the definitive autonomous revenue operating system for B2B teams of every size — replacing fragmented stacks of 6–10 point tools with one platform where AI agents, 700M+ verified buyers, a native CRM, a built-in CDP, multichannel sales engagement, voice AI, content generation, and expert GTM services all share a single buyer graph. Every revenue role — from SDR to CRO, from RevOps to Customer Success — works from one source of truth, priced by execution rather than seats, making programmable revenue the new standard for how B2B companies grow.

## Brand Essence

**Tagline:** Revenue is programmable. Run it on one graph.
**Brand Promise:** graph8 promises to replace your entire GTM stack with one autonomous revenue system — where AI agents do the prospecting, outreach, qualification, and follow-up; a native CRM tracks every deal; a built-in CDP unifies every data source; and your reps step in only for the live human moments that win the relationship.
**Unique Value:** graph8 is the only platform that unifies 15+ specialized AI agents, a 7-app sales engagement suite, a native CRM with quote-to-cash, a 700M+ contact buyer graph, real-time intent signals, a built-in CDP with 500+ connectors, AI voice agents, agent twins, content generation via Studio, workflow automation, developer APIs, and vetted GTM services — all on one shared buyer graph, priced by execution rather than per-seat licenses.

## Core Values

### Item 1

**Value:** One Graph, One Truth
**Meaning:** Every product, agent, and workflow in graph8 reads from and writes to a single buyer graph. There is no siloed data, no reconciliation across tools, and no version of the truth that conflicts with another. This architectural conviction shapes every product decision.
**Behaviors:**
- All 19 products share the same buyer record
- Agent actions are logged to revenue memory so every subsequent agent and human sees the full history
- Two-way CRM sync ensures the buyer graph stays current whether the team uses HubSpot, Salesforce, or graph8's native CRM
- Contact deduplication and identity resolution happen in real time across anonymous and known visitors


### Item 2

**Value:** Agents Do the Work, Humans Win the Moment
**Meaning:** graph8 believes AI agents should carry the volume — prospecting, sequencing, enriching, qualifying, drafting, logging — so human reps can focus exclusively on the live conversations and relationship moments that machines cannot replace. Automation is not the goal; freeing humans to do what humans do best is.
**Behaviors:**
- 15 named AI agents autonomously handle SDR work, deal management, customer success monitoring, content creation, and revenue operations
- My Desk surfaces only the deals that need a human decision today, ranked by urgency and deal value
- Agent Twins cover reps 24/7 in their own voice and tone, handing back to the human the moment a buyer wants to talk
- Human approval gates can be inserted at any workflow step, keeping humans in control of high-stakes decisions


### Item 3

**Value:** Execution Over Access
**Meaning:** graph8 charges for what the system actually does — sending, calling, enriching, booking, generating — not for how many people can log in. This pricing philosophy is a values statement: revenue software should reward outcomes, not penalize growth by taxing headcount.
**Behaviors:**
- Unlimited users on every plan with no per-seat fees
- 700M+ contacts and 100M+ companies are free to search and browse
- Execution credits are consumed only when graph8 performs real work: sends, calls, enrichments, AI generation, bookings, and agent runs
- The Data Tax Calculator quantifies what teams overpay for access at competing platforms


### Item 4

**Value:** Built on Real Revenue, Not Theory
**Meaning:** graph8's AI agents, playbooks, buyer graph, and intent signals are grounded in 10 years of real CIENCE B2B outbound campaign data across thousands of brands and millions of conversations. This heritage is a core value, not a marketing claim — it means every default, every recommendation, and every agent behavior reflects what actually works in real sales motion.
**Behaviors:**
- The octa GTM model and octa squared algorithms are trained on decade-long real campaign outcomes
- Studio generates ICPs, messaging, and sequences informed by real outbound patterns
- GTM Services draws on vetted operators who have run real campaigns, not consultants with theoretical frameworks
- The Programmable Revenue Community publishes weekly research grounded in Tenbound GTM benchmarking data


### Item 5

**Value:** Governed Autonomy
**Meaning:** Autonomous AI systems are only trustworthy when every action is logged, auditable, and reversible. graph8 believes that automation at scale requires governance at every layer — approval queues, revenue memory, audit trails, and human-in-the-loop controls — so teams can deploy AI agents with confidence rather than anxiety.
**Behaviors:**
- Every agent and human action is written to an append-only revenue memory log
- Workflows support optional human approval gates at any step
- The Control and Safety agent manages approval workflows for high-stakes autonomous actions
- Enterprise deployments include SSO, RBAC, regional data residency, SOC 2 Type II certification, and SIEM-exportable audit logs


## Personality Traits

### Item 1

**Trait:** Confident and Direct
**Description:** graph8 speaks with the authority of a platform built on a decade of real revenue outcomes. It does not hedge, over-qualify, or hide behind vague claims. It states what it does, how it works, and what it costs — clearly and without fuss.
**Examples:**
- 'Revenue is programmable. Run it on one graph.'
- 'Pay for execution, not seats.'
- 'Your reps close deals. The CRM fills itself.'
- Pricing pages show exact credit costs rather than 'contact us for pricing'


### Item 2

**Trait:** Technically Precise
**Description:** graph8 respects the intelligence of its audience — sales engineers, RevOps leaders, developers, and founders who can smell vague marketing from a distance. It names the specific product, the exact capability, and the precise mechanism rather than retreating to buzzwords.
**Examples:**
- Product pages name specific agent behaviors: 'The Deal Agent preps each card before you open it'
- Developer documentation specifies '54 REST resources, 460 operations, OpenAPI 3.1.0'
- Integrations are listed by name: HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, ClickHouse, Snowflake, BigQuery
- Signal counts are specific: '~2 billion buying signals a day'


### Item 3

**Trait:** Human at the Center
**Description:** Despite being an AI-first platform, graph8's brand voice consistently celebrates the human rep, the human relationship, and the human moment. AI is framed as a tool that serves people, not replaces them. This creates warmth and trust in a category prone to dehumanizing automation rhetoric.
**Examples:**
- 'The volume is the machine's. The deal and the relationship stay yours.'
- 'AI runs the volume. You win the room.'
- My Desk is designed around the rep's daily experience, not the manager's reporting view
- Agent Twins hand back to the human 'the moment a buyer wants to talk'


## Primary Audience

**Segment:** B2B Revenue & Sales Leaders
**Description:** VP of Sales, CROs, Revenue Operations leaders, and Sales Development leaders at mid-market to enterprise B2B companies who are responsible for driving predictable pipeline and revenue growth. These buyers are overwhelmed by a fragmented stack of point solutions — separate CRMs, data vendors, sequencers, dialers, and AI tools — and are actively seeking a unified platform that can consolidate their revenue technology and automate workflows end-to-end.
**Needs:**
- Consolidated revenue tech stack to reduce tool sprawl and cost
- AI-driven automation to scale outbound prospecting and SDR workflows
- Accurate, enriched B2B contact and account data to fuel targeting
- End-to-end pipeline visibility from prospecting through close and renewal
- Faster time-to-revenue with less manual effort from sales reps
- Reliable forecasting and at-risk deal detection to protect quota attainment


## Secondary Audiences

### Developers and GTM Engineers Building Revenue Applications

**Segment:** Developers and GTM Engineers Building Revenue Applications
**Description:** Technical builders — whether in-house GTM engineers, indie developers, or AI-native product teams — who want to build revenue applications on top of graph8's infrastructure rather than operate the platform as a GTM user. They interact through the REST API (460 operations, OpenAPI 3.1), JavaScript SDK (25+ modules), MCP server (150+ tools for Claude/Cursor/ChatGPT), and CLI (143 commands).
**Needs:**
- Bearer-authenticated REST API with predictable envelope responses and cursor pagination
- MCP server for wiring AI agents (Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT) directly to the buyer graph
- SDK with typed requests, automatic retries, and webhook signature verification
- Free search and browse of 700M+ contacts without burning credits
- Production-grade primitives for enrichment, sequences, inbox, meetings, voice, and CRM


### Solopreneurs and Founder-Led Startups

**Segment:** Solopreneurs and Founder-Led Startups
**Description:** Individual founders and early-stage teams who are simultaneously the product builder, the marketer, and the seller. They need an autonomous revenue motion that runs itself while they focus on product — one that can be stood up in a single session from a URL, without needing a RevOps hire or a six-tool stack.
**Needs:**
- Studio to generate ICP, messaging, landing pages, and sequences from a single URL
- AI agents that prospect, sequence, qualify, and book autonomously on autopilot
- Configurable autonomy lanes (Manual / Hybrid / Autopilot) per agent and per channel
- Free contact search and intent signals to identify in-market buyers without a data contract
- Unlimited users with no per-seat fees from day one


### GTM Agencies Running Client Campaigns

**Segment:** GTM Agencies Running Client Campaigns
**Description:** Agencies and outsourced SDR firms managing outbound, demand generation, and SDR-as-a-service for multiple clients simultaneously. They need per-client buyer graphs, multi-domain deliverability, isolated governance, and the ability to run many client brands in parallel without separate tool stacks for each.
**Needs:**
- Agency API keys and cross-org targeting for multi-client management
- Per-client ICPs, brand voices, and messaging frameworks generated via Studio
- Multi-domain email infrastructure with deliverability managed by graph8
- Isolated data governance and reporting per client
- Talent Marketplace to hire additional vetted GTM operators at zero markup


**Market Position:** graph8 occupies the position of the Autonomous Revenue Operating System — a category it defines against the fragmented landscape of point tools (Apollo for data, Outreach for sequences, Salesforce for CRM, 6sense for intent, Segment for CDP, Gong for conversation intelligence, Clay for enrichment, Drift for chat). Where competitors each own one layer of the revenue stack and force teams to stitch them together with integrations, RevOps headcount, and reconciliation work, graph8 unifies all layers — buyer data, intent signals, sales engagement, AI agents, CRM, CDP, content generation, voice AI, workflow automation, and developer APIs — on a single buyer graph. Its pricing model (execution-based, unlimited users) further differentiates it from per-seat vendors whose cost structures penalize team growth. graph8 is positioned above pure-play AI SDR tools (Artisan, 11x) by offering the full revenue stack, above pure-play sales engagement platforms (Outreach, Salesloft) by including native CRM, data, and AI agents, and above pure-play data platforms (ZoomInfo, Apollo) by including the execution layer that activates the data.

## Key Differentiators

- One Buyer Graph Architecture: Every product — Agents, Applications, CRM, Data, Signals, Studio, Data Pipelines, Desktop, Work, Integrations, Voice AI, Agent Twins, Workbench, Workflows, AI Receptionist, Talent Marketplace — reads from and writes to a single unified buyer graph, eliminating data silos, reconciliation, and integration maintenance across tools.
- 15 Specialized AI Agents Across Every Revenue Role: Named agents (SDR Agent, Deal Agent, CSM Agent, Content Agent, CRO Copilot, Agent Twins, AI Receptionist, Voice AI, and more) autonomously run specific revenue workflows — not generic AI copilots, but purpose-built agents trained for defined jobs with governed approval gates.
- Execution-Based Pricing with Unlimited Users: graph8 charges for what the system executes (sends, calls, enrichments, bookings, AI generation) rather than for seats. The entire platform — all apps, all agents, all data — is available to unlimited users on the Team plan, eliminating the per-seat tax that competing platforms impose.
- 700M+ Contact Buyer Graph Free to Search: The broadest B2B contact and company database in the platform is free to browse on every plan, with ~30 billion intent signals refreshed continuously. Competing platforms charge for every lookup and reveal.
- Built-In CDP and Data Pipelines with 500+ Connectors: Unlike platforms that require a separate Segment or RudderStack contract, graph8 includes a full Customer Data Platform with JavaScript event transformation, schema governance, identity resolution, reverse ETL, and 500+ source and destination connectors natively.
- AI Voice Agents and Agent Twins with Voice Cloning: graph8 includes Voice AI that makes and receives calls, qualifies leads live, and books meetings — plus Agent Twins that clone individual reps' voices and writing styles to cover them 24/7, capabilities absent from most sales engagement competitors.
- Grounded in 10 Years of Real CIENCE Campaign Data: Every AI model, playbook, and agent behavior is trained on real B2B outbound outcomes across thousands of brands and millions of conversations — not synthetic training data — giving graph8 an empirical advantage over platforms built on theoretical assumptions.
- Full Developer Platform with MCP, REST API, SDK, and CLI: graph8 exposes its entire buyer graph, engagement suite, CRM, and agent infrastructure as programmable primitives via 150+ MCP tools, 460 REST operations (OpenAPI 3.1), a typed JavaScript SDK, and 143 CLI commands — enabling AI-native teams to build revenue applications without standing up their own infrastructure.
- Studio: Strategy to Live Campaign in One Session: Studio generates 44 intelligence documents (brand guidelines, ICPs, persona libraries, messaging frameworks, competitive positioning) from a single URL, then produces deployable campaign assets — sequences, landing pages, ad copy, newsletters, battlecards — all in brand voice and directly launchable from the same platform.
- Vetted GTM Talent Marketplace and Expert Services: Beyond software, graph8 offers access to vetted GTM operators at zero markup and expert GTM Services for teams that need human implementation support, strategy, or campaign execution alongside the platform — combining SaaS with managed services in one ecosystem.

**Origin Story:** graph8 was built on a decade of real B2B outbound campaign data generated by CIENCE, one of the world's largest sales development organizations. While other platforms were built on synthetic assumptions about what works, graph8 was forged in the reality of millions of conversations, thousands of campaigns, and measurable pipeline outcomes across enterprise, software, finance, and services. That operational heritage — combined with the GTM benchmarking and research of Tenbound — gave graph8 an unfair advantage: its AI agents, playbooks, and buyer graph are trained on real-world revenue motion, not theory. In 2024, that decade of learning became a platform.

**Brand Narrative:** B2B revenue teams are drowning in point tools. The average team pays for a data vendor, a sequencer, a dialer, a CRM, an intent platform, a CDP, a content tool, and a chat platform — eight separate contracts, eight separate logins, eight separate data models that never quite agree with each other. RevOps exists largely to maintain the plumbing between them. And even after all that investment, the buyer graph is still fragmented, the CRM is still stale, and reps still spend more time updating records than talking to buyers.

graph8 was built to end that. Not by adding another point tool, but by replacing the entire stack with a single autonomous revenue system built on one buyer graph.

The buyer graph is the foundation: 700M+ verified B2B contacts, 100M+ companies, 30 billion intent signals, and website visitor identity — all free to search, continuously refreshed, and shared across every surface. When a buyer signal fires — a pricing page visit, a hiring post, a job change, a competitor evaluation — graph8 resolves it to a real person, scores it against your ICP, and launches the work automatically.

The work is done by 15 specialized AI agents: SDR Agents that prospect and sequence, Deal Agents that prep briefs and draft next steps, CSM Agents that watch health scores and flag churn risk 90 days before the renewal call, Voice AI agents that make and receive calls and book meetings live, Agent Twins that cover reps in their own voice around the clock, Content Agents that generate brand-consistent campaigns from a single URL. Every agent action is logged to revenue memory — auditable, reversible, and visible to every subsequent agent and human who touches that account.

When a buyer is ready to talk, the work reaches your rep with the full account history already attached. My Desk ranks their day by deal urgency and signal strength. The CRM fills itself from every call and email. Forecasts roll up live from the deals reps actually work. Quotes flow to e-sign and billing automatically. The human rep walks into every conversation fully briefed, sharper than the buyer, focused entirely on the relationship moment that machines cannot replace.

For teams that need their data infrastructure unified, graph8's built-in CDP ingests 500+ data sources, runs real-time JavaScript transformations, resolves anonymous and known identity, and activates every event across sequences, campaigns, segments, and reports — without a separate Segment or RudderStack contract. For developers and AI-native teams, the entire buyer graph and engagement suite is exposed as programmable primitives via MCP, REST API, SDK, and CLI.

And for teams that need human expertise alongside the platform, graph8's GTM Services connects them with vetted operators at zero markup, and the Programmable Revenue Community delivers weekly research and benchmarking every Tuesday.

All of it — the agents, the apps, the CRM, the data, the CDP, the voice AI, the content engine, the talent marketplace — runs on one buyer graph, priced by what the system executes, not by how many people can log in.

Revenue is programmable. graph8 is the system you run it on.

And even after all that investment, the buyer graph is still fragmented, the CRM is still stale, and reps still spend more time updating records than talking to buyers.

graph8 was built to end that. Not by adding another point tool, but by replacing the entire stack with a single autonomous revenue system built on one buyer graph.

The buyer graph is the foundation: 700M+ verified B2B contacts, 100M+ companies, 30 billion intent signals, and website visitor identity — all free to search, continuously refreshed, and shared across every surface. When a buyer signal fires — a pricing page visit, a hiring post, a job change, a competitor evaluation — graph8 resolves it to a real person, scores it against your ICP, and launches the work automatically.

The work is done by 15 specialized AI agents: SDR Agents that prospect and sequence, Deal Agents that prep briefs and draft next steps, CSM Agents that watch health scores and flag churn risk 90 days before the renewal call, Voice AI agents that make and receive calls and book meetings live, Agent Twins that cover reps in their own voice around the clock, Content Agents that generate brand-consistent campaigns from a single URL. Every agent action is logged to revenue memory — auditable, reversible, and visible to every subsequent agent and human who touches that account.

When a buyer is ready to talk, the work reaches your rep with the full account history already attached. My Desk ranks their day by deal urgency and signal strength. The CRM fills itself from every call and email. Forecasts roll up live from the deals reps actually work. Quotes flow to e-sign and billing automatically. The human rep walks into every conversation fully briefed, sharper than the buyer, focused entirely on the relationship moment that machines cannot replace.

For teams that need their data infrastructure unified, graph8's built-in CDP ingests 500+ data sources, runs real-time JavaScript transformations, resolves anonymous and known identity, and activates every event across sequences, campaigns, segments, and reports — without a separate Segment or RudderStack contract. For developers and AI-native teams, the entire buyer graph and engagement suite is exposed as programmable primitives via MCP, REST API, SDK, and CLI.

And for teams that need human expertise alongside the platform, graph8's GTM Services connects them with vetted operators at zero markup, and the Programmable Revenue Community delivers weekly research and benchmarking every Tuesday.

All of it — the agents, the apps, the CRM, the data, the CDP, the voice AI, the content engine, the talent marketplace — runs on one buyer graph, priced by what the system executes, not by how many people can log in.

Revenue is programmable. graph8 is the system you run it on.

# Brand Voice

**Voice Summary:** graph8 speaks like a seasoned revenue operator who has run thousands of real B2B campaigns and has nothing to prove. The voice is precise, direct, and grounded in execution — it names the specific problem, states the specific fix, and moves on. There is no filler, no hype, and no vague promises. graph8 treats its audience as intelligent practitioners — SDRs, AEs, RevOps leads, CROs, developers, and founders — who can spot a generic claim from a mile away and who respect specificity above all else. The tone is confident without being arrogant, modern without being flippant, and technical without being inaccessible. graph8 consistently frames AI and automation as a force that amplifies human judgment at the live moment, never as a replacement for it. Copy leads with outcomes and concrete mechanics ("The CRM fills itself," "Buyer motion starts the work"), uses short declarative sentences as anchors, and earns trust through transparency — including honest framing of what is free, what costs credits, and what requires human approval. Across every surface — from homepage headlines to developer docs to sales role pages — the voice maintains the same operating posture: unhurried, precise, and unambiguously on the side of the person doing the revenue work.

## Voice In Three Words

- Precise
- Autonomous
- Practitioner

## Tone Attributes

### Direct

**Attribute:** Direct
**Scale Position:** Blunt but never abrasive
**Description:** graph8 leads every sentence with the point. No wind-up, no hedging, no throat-clearing. Headlines state the outcome first ('Your reps close deals. The CRM fills itself.'). Body copy explains the mechanism immediately after. Qualifiers are used only when they add precision, never to soften a claim.

### Confident

**Attribute:** Confident
**Scale Position:** Assured but never boastful
**Description:** graph8 speaks from a decade of real B2B outbound data (the CIENCE heritage) and lets that track record do the heavy lifting. Confidence shows up as specificity — '700M contacts, 100M companies, 30B intent signals' — rather than superlatives. The brand never needs to say it is the best; it shows what it does and lets the reader draw the conclusion.

### Human-first

**Attribute:** Human-first
**Scale Position:** Warm toward the operator, never sentimental
**Description:** graph8 consistently positions the human rep, AE, founder, or developer as the protagonist. AI agents are the support crew. Language like 'You win the room' and 'The deal and the relationship stay yours' reinforces that the platform exists to amplify human judgment, not eliminate it. The voice respects the reader's intelligence and their craft.

### Technically fluent

**Attribute:** Technically fluent
**Scale Position:** Expert without being exclusionary
**Description:** graph8 speaks naturally about APIs, MCP servers, buyer graphs, intent signals, CDPs, and revenue memory without stopping to explain every term to a novice. When writing for developers or RevOps, the tone goes deeper into mechanics. When writing for founders or sales reps, it stays at the outcome layer. The fluency shifts register by audience without ever dumbing down.

## Voice Characteristics

### Item 1

**Characteristic:** Short declarative anchors
**Definition:** graph8 opens sections and headlines with short, complete sentences that state a fact or outcome. These anchors set the operating premise before any elaboration follows.
**Do Example:** Buyer motion starts the work. graph8 brings every buying signal together — around 2 billion a day — resolves each to a real person, and starts a launch automatically.
**Dont Example:** graph8's innovative, AI-powered platform is designed to help modern revenue teams unlock unprecedented value by leveraging real-time buyer intent data across multiple channels.

### Item 2

**Characteristic:** Mechanics over marketing
**Definition:** graph8 describes how things work, not just what they do. Specific numbers, named components, and step-by-step flows replace vague benefit statements.
**Do Example:** Every call, email, and meeting logs itself. Native deals, quote to cash, and a forecast off live data — all on one buyer graph — so your AEs work the right deal instead of updating records.
**Dont Example:** Our AI-powered CRM transforms how your team manages customer relationships and drives smarter, more efficient revenue outcomes at scale.

### Item 3

**Characteristic:** The human node framing
**Definition:** graph8 consistently reserves the highest-value moments — the live call, the close, the relationship — for the human. Automation is framed as clearing the path, not replacing the person.
**Do Example:** AI agents run the work. Your reps win the moment. When a buyer is ready to talk, the call reaches your rep with the account history already on it.
**Dont Example:** Our AI handles your entire sales process from start to finish so your team can focus on other priorities.

### Item 4

**Characteristic:** Role-specific precision
**Definition:** graph8 names the exact role it is speaking to and addresses the specific pain that role lives with daily, not a generic revenue team problem.
**Do Example:** Open graph8 and the cockpit has already ranked the three deals that need a move today, weighted by stage risk, deal value, and signal strength. No staring at a pipeline list wondering where to start.
**Dont Example:** graph8 helps all members of your go-to-market organization work more effectively and make better decisions using real-time data.

### Item 5

**Characteristic:** Transparency as credibility
**Definition:** graph8 states what is free, what costs credits, and what requires human approval. This honesty is baked into the voice and builds trust with skeptical practitioners.
**Do Example:** Search is free. Pay only when graph8 executes the work for you. Credits move when graph8 does something on your behalf — a sequence sent, a call placed, a meeting booked.
**Dont Example:** Get started today and experience the full power of graph8 with our flexible, value-aligned pricing model built for teams of every size.

### Item 6

**Characteristic:** Heritage grounding
**Definition:** graph8 references its CIENCE heritage — a decade of real B2B outbound — to substantiate claims. This is positioned as a source of the platform's trained playbooks, not as a generic credential.
**Do Example:** The playbooks learned from a decade of real outbound. graph8's revenue motion is shaped by the CIENCE archive: ten years of real B2B outbound across thousands of campaigns and millions of conversations.
**Dont Example:** Backed by years of industry experience, graph8 brings deep expertise to every customer engagement.

## Writing Principles

### Item 1

**Principle:** Lead with the outcome, follow with the mechanism
**Explanation:** Readers decide in the first sentence whether a section is worth their time. graph8 earns that time by stating the outcome — 'The CRM fills itself,' 'Your desktop runs itself,' 'From strategy to a live campaign in one session' — then immediately explaining how the system achieves it. This sequence respects the reader's time and builds credibility simultaneously.
**Guidelines:**
- Open headlines with the end state the reader wants, not with product features
- Follow the outcome statement with the specific mechanism in the next 1-2 sentences
- Avoid burying the lead in context or background before stating the value
- Use present tense for outcomes to make them feel immediate and real


### Item 2

**Principle:** Be specific enough to be believed
**Explanation:** graph8's audience — revenue practitioners — are deeply skeptical of vague claims. Specificity is the primary trust signal. Numbers, named components, and concrete sequences ('8 API calls from signal to qualified meeting') carry more weight than any superlative.
**Guidelines:**
- Use real numbers from the platform wherever available (700M contacts, 100M companies, 30B signals, 2B signals/day, 500+ connectors, 150+ MCP tools)
- Name specific agents, modules, and workflows rather than referring generically to 'AI' or 'automation'
- Describe concrete step sequences rather than abstract capabilities
- Avoid 'industry-leading,' 'best-in-class,' 'powerful,' and other unverifiable superlatives


### Item 3

**Principle:** Write for the practitioner at the moment of decision
**Explanation:** graph8 content is read by people in the middle of real work — a rep preparing for a call, a RevOps lead evaluating a stack consolidation, a developer integrating an API. The voice meets them at that moment with the exact information they need, nothing more.
**Guidelines:**
- Match the depth of explanation to the reader's role and context (deeper mechanics for developers and RevOps, outcome focus for reps and founders)
- Keep sentences short when writing for scan-heavy contexts like hero sections and nav copy
- Use bullet structure to surface the most decision-relevant information quickly
- Eliminate preamble — never start with 'In today's competitive landscape' or similar throat-clearing


### Item 4

**Principle:** Position AI as the force multiplier, humans as the irreplaceable node
**Explanation:** graph8's central editorial stance is that AI agents carry the volume so humans can operate at their highest leverage — the live call, the close, the relationship. This framing must be consistent across all product areas, from the sequencer to the CRM to the developer platform.
**Guidelines:**
- Always name what the agent does AND what the human does in the same context
- Reserve language like 'you win,' 'you close,' 'you decide' for human actions
- Never imply that automation eliminates the need for the human at any stage
- Reinforce that humans control the autonomy level ('you set the leash per agent')


### Item 5

**Principle:** One system, one graph — reinforce the unified architecture
**Explanation:** The buyer graph is graph8's core architectural differentiator. Every product description, role page, and feature explanation should reinforce that all components — agents, CRM, data, signals, Studio, pipelines — read and write to one shared record. This counters the 'hairball' of disconnected point tools.
**Guidelines:**
- Reference the buyer graph when introducing any platform component
- Use phrases like 'on one buyer graph,' 'the same record,' 'one source of truth,' and 'one buyer graph across your whole stack' consistently
- Contrast the unified architecture against fragmented stacks without naming specific competitors
- Show how data flows between components rather than treating each feature in isolation


### Item 6

**Principle:** Earn trust through transparent pricing language
**Explanation:** graph8's pricing model — free search, execution-based credits, unlimited users — is a genuine differentiator. The voice communicates this model plainly and repeatedly, using it as proof of the brand's alignment with the customer's interests rather than as fine print.
**Guidelines:**
- State 'free' for search, data browsing, and contact exploration clearly and early in relevant contexts
- Always explain what triggers a credit charge (sends, calls, agent runs, enrichments, meeting bookings)
- Use 'pay for execution, not seats' as a consistent framing anchor
- Never obscure or soften the credit model — transparency here builds trust, not skepticism


## Channel Guidance

### Item 1

**Channel:** Website (Product & Role Pages)
**Tone Adjustments:** Full precision mode. Headlines are short declaratives stating the outcome. Body copy names the specific mechanism immediately. Role pages speak directly to the named role's daily pain. Platform pages show how each component connects to the buyer graph. Every page maintains the human-node framing.
**Key Considerations:**
- Lead every section with the outcome, not the feature name
- Use specifics: agent names, credit model details, exact data counts
- Reinforce the one-buyer-graph architecture across all product descriptions
- Include the free/credits distinction on any page where pricing context is relevant
- Avoid multi-paragraph explanations of concepts the audience already understands


### Item 2

**Channel:** Email (Outreach & Nurture)
**Tone Adjustments:** Tighter and more personal than website copy. The first sentence must earn the second. Subject lines are declarative or curiosity-gap, never clickbait. Body copy references a specific signal or context (hiring data, intent spike, role change) to demonstrate that the outreach is informed, not generic. Short paragraphs, clear single ask.
**Key Considerations:**
- Open with a specific reason to reach out — not a generic intro
- Reference the buyer's context before introducing graph8's capability
- One CTA per email, stated plainly and early enough to be seen without scrolling
- Match the register to the recipient's role (more technical for developers and RevOps, outcome-focused for sales leaders and founders)
- Never use 'just checking in' or 'circling back' — acknowledge why you are reaching out specifically


### Item 3

**Channel:** LinkedIn
**Tone Adjustments:** Slightly more expansive than email — LinkedIn allows for a setup before the payoff. Posts can open with a contrarian observation, a specific data point, or a named scenario from the revenue practitioner world. The voice stays direct and practitioner-first. No motivational filler. Engagement is earned through insight, not virality tactics.
**Key Considerations:**
- Open with a sentence that earns a click to 'see more' — a specific observation, not a vague teaser
- Build to one clear point or takeaway per post
- Reference real product mechanics or CIENCE heritage data to substantiate claims
- Avoid listicles with generic items; if using a list, make every item specific and non-obvious
- CTA should feel like a natural next step, not a hard sell


### Item 4

**Channel:** Developer & API Documentation
**Tone Adjustments:** The most technical register graph8 uses. Precision is paramount — every parameter, return value, and error code is named exactly. Explanatory prose is minimal and purpose-driven: it tells the developer what to do and why, then gets out of the way. Worked examples are preferred over abstract descriptions. The voice acknowledges that the developer is capable and treats every instruction as a peer-to-peer handoff.
**Key Considerations:**
- Lead with what the endpoint or method does, then show the example immediately
- Use consistent naming conventions that match the API contract exactly
- Flag credit-charging operations clearly so developers can build billing logic
- Include error cases and edge conditions — omitting them is not simplicity, it is incompleteness
- The 'you' in developer docs refers to the developer building the integration, not an end user


### Item 5

**Channel:** Sales Calls & Demos
**Tone Adjustments:** Conversational and diagnostic. The graph8 rep should sound like someone who has studied the prospect's stack and signal activity before the call — because they have. Questions are specific, not generic discovery scripts. Explanations of the platform prioritize the component most relevant to the prospect's named pain. The human-node framing is especially important here: always acknowledge what the rep's team does well and position graph8 as clearing the path for more of it.
**Key Considerations:**
- Reference the buyer's specific context (role, company size, likely stack) early in the call
- Use the platform's own language naturally — 'buyer graph,' 'launch,' 'signals' — but define briefly if the prospect seems unfamiliar
- Anchor the value conversation in the data-tax framing when stack consolidation is the use case
- Let specifics do the work: exact credit costs, named agents, real workflow sequences
- Close with a concrete next step that mirrors how graph8 itself operates — decisive, logged, and briefed


## Word Choice

**Preferred Words:**
- execute
- launch
- run
- motion
- signal
- graph
- buyer graph
- pipeline
- close
- briefed
- ranked
- logged
- resolved
- unified
- one system
- one record
- agent
- rep
- operator
- practitioner
- live moment
- human node
- free to search
- credits
- execution
- context
- precise
- real
- verified
- live
- act on
- autonomy
- govern
- audit

**Avoided Words:**
- powerful
- robust
- seamless
- synergies
- game-changing
- revolutionary
- disruptive
- innovative
- cutting-edge
- best-in-class
- industry-leading
- unlock
- leverage
- holistic
- end-to-end solution
- empower
- transformative
- world-class
- bleeding-edge
- next-generation
- reimagine
- ecosystem
- scalable solutions
- touch base
- circle back
- boil the ocean
- move the needle

**Jargon Policy:** graph8 uses GTM and sales technology terminology fluently because its audience lives in this world. Terms like buyer graph, intent signals, ICP, sequencer, MCP, CDP, waterfall enrichment, and revenue memory are used without apology on product and role pages. However, jargon is never stacked for its own sake — each technical term must carry its weight by being the most precise word for the concept. On pages targeting founders, solopreneurs, or non-technical decision-makers, the voice shifts to outcome language and introduces technical terms only when necessary, with brief inline context.
**Acronym Policy:** Standard GTM acronyms (SDR, AE, CRM, ICP, RevOps, GTM, CRO, CSM, ABM, MCP, CDP, API, SDK, CLI) are used freely without definition on product, role, and solution pages — the audience knows them. On introductory or educational pages (AI training, free data, solopreneurs), spell out less common acronyms on first use. Never use acronyms as a shortcut to avoid explaining a concept properly.

## Grammar Preferences

- Use second-person singular ('you,' 'your') throughout — graph8 speaks directly to the individual practitioner, not 'teams' or 'organizations' as abstract entities
- Present tense for product behaviors ('The CRM fills itself,' 'Signals watch intent') to make capabilities feel immediate
- Active voice is the default; passive voice is used only when the agent performing the action is intentionally unknown or irrelevant
- Sentence fragments are acceptable in headlines and hero copy when they create punch ('One buyer graph. Every channel. One bill.')
- Oxford comma is used in all lists
- Numbers under 10 are written as numerals when they refer to quantities of platform components, steps, or credits (e.g., '3 deals,' '8 API calls') to maintain the precise, data-forward tone
- Spell out numbers when they begin a sentence
- Periods end all bullet points that form complete sentences; no periods on fragments used as labels or nav items

## Formatting Guidelines

- Use short declarative sentences (8–14 words) as section and headline anchors, followed by longer explanatory sentences
- Bullet lists should use concrete, parallel construction — each bullet begins with a past-tense verb (logged, ranked, drafted, resolved) or a checkmark (✓) for feature confirmations
- Bold is used for named agents, key outcomes, and the most critical phrase in a paragraph — not for decoration
- Code snippets, command-line examples, and API references use monospace formatting on developer-facing pages
- Numbered sequences (01, 02, 03) are used to show workflow steps and build the sense of a predictable, repeatable system
- Section labels like 'The autonomous revenue system' and 'For sales reps and AEs' are used as eyebrow text above headlines to set context without burying it in the headline itself
- CTAs use active verbs and concrete framing: 'Start Free,' 'Get API key,' 'See the use cases' — never 'Learn More' or 'Discover'
- Avoid exclamation marks in product and feature copy; confidence comes from precision, not punctuation
- Em dashes are used to separate a short declarative from its elaboration within a single sentence

**Audience Adaptations:** graph8 serves distinctly different audiences with the same underlying voice, shifting register and depth without shifting personality. For sales reps and AEs, the voice leads with daily workflow relief — ranked queues, call briefs, logged admin — and frames graph8 as the thing that makes every rep operate like the best rep. For RevOps and Marketing Ops, it goes deeper into architecture — field mapping, reconciliation, audit logs, the hairball problem — and speaks the language of system governance. For revenue leaders (CROs, VP Sales, Founders), it centers on the forecast, the operating cadence, and the ability to coach from real data. For developers and builders, it shifts to API mechanics, SDK modules, MCP tool counts, and credit metering logic — the voice becomes peer-to-peer and code-first. For startups and solopreneurs, it emphasizes speed-to-launch, the free data layer, and the autonomy controls that let one person run a full revenue motion. For enterprise buyers, it surfaces governance, compliance posture (SOC 2 Type II, SAML, regional residency), and the revenue memory audit trail. Across all audiences, the core voice attributes — direct, precise, human-first — remain constant. What adapts is the technical depth, the named pain, and the specific product components brought to the foreground.

Copy leads with outcomes and concrete mechanics ("The CRM fills itself," "Buyer motion starts the work"), uses short declarative sentences as anchors, and earns trust through transparency — including honest framing of what is free, what costs credits, and what requires human approval. Across every surface — from homepage headlines to developer docs to sales role pages — the voice maintains the same operating posture: unhurried, precise, and unambiguously on the side of the person doing the revenue work.

graph8 speaks from a decade of real B2B outbound data (the CIENCE heritage) and lets that track record do the heavy lifting. writing_principles.principle: Lead with the outcome, follow with the mechanism

writing_principles.principle: Be specific enough to be believed

Describe concrete step sequences rather than abstract capabilities

writing_principles.explanation: graph8's audience — revenue practitioners — are deeply skeptical of vague claims. Specificity is the primary trust signal. Numbers, named components, and concrete sequences ('8 API calls from signal to qualified meeting') carry more weight than any superlative.

writing_principles.principle: Write for the practitioner at the moment of decision
guidelines: Match the depth of explanation to the reader's role and context (deeper mechanics for developers and RevOps, outcome focus for reps and founders)
Keep sentences short when writing for scan-heavy contexts like hero sections and nav copy
Use bullet structure to surface the most decision-relevant information quickly
Eliminate preamble — never start with 'In today's competitive landscape' or similar throat-clearing
writing_principles.explanation: graph8 content is read by people in the middle of real work — a rep preparing for a call, a RevOps lead evaluating a stack consolidation, a developer integrating an API. The voice meets them at that moment with the exact information they need, nothing more.

writing_principles.principle: Position AI as the force multiplier, humans as the irreplaceable node

writing_principles.principle: One system, one graph — reinforce the unified architecture

Every product description, role page, and feature explanation should reinforce that all components — agents, CRM, data, signals, Studio, pipelines — read and write to one shared record. guidelines: State 'free' for search, data browsing, and contact exploration clearly and early in relevant contexts

grammar_preferences: Use second-person singular ('you,' 'your') throughout — graph8 speaks directly to the individual practitioner, not 'teams' or 'organizations' as abstract entities
Present tense for product behaviors ('The CRM fills itself,' 'Signals watch intent') to make capabilities feel immediate
Active voice is the default; passive voice is used only when the agent performing the action is intentionally unknown or irrelevant
Sentence fragments are acceptable in headlines and hero copy when they create punch ('One buyer graph. Every channel. One bill.')
Oxford comma is used in all lists
Numbers under 10 are written as numerals when they refer to quantities of platform components, steps, or credits (e.g., '3 deals,' '8 API calls') to maintain the precise, data-forward tone
Spell out numbers when they begin a sentence
Periods end all bullet points that form complete sentences; no periods on fragments used as labels or nav items
structured_data.audience_adaptations: graph8 serves distinctly different audiences with the same underlying voice, shifting register and depth without shifting personality. For sales reps and AEs, the voice leads with daily workflow relief — ranked queues, call briefs, logged admin — and frames graph8 as the thing that makes every rep operate like the best rep. For RevOps and Marketing Ops, it goes deeper into architecture — field mapping, reconciliation, audit logs, the hairball problem — and speaks the language of system governance. For revenue leaders (CROs, VP Sales, Founders), it centers on the forecast, the operating cadence, and the ability to coach from real data. For developers and builders, it shifts to API mechanics, SDK modules, MCP tool counts, and credit metering logic — the voice becomes peer-to-peer and code-first. For startups and solopreneurs, it emphasizes speed-to-launch, the free data layer, and the autonomy controls that let one person run a full revenue motion. For enterprise buyers, it surfaces governance, compliance posture (SOC 2 Type II, SAML, regional residency), and the revenue memory audit trail. Across all audiences, the core voice attributes — direct, precise, human-first — remain constant. What adapts is the technical depth, the named pain, and the specific product components brought to the foreground.
formatting_guidelines: Use short declarative sentences (8–14 words) as section and headline anchors, followed by longer explanatory sentences
Bullet lists should use concrete, parallel construction — each bullet begins with a past-tense verb (logged, ranked, drafted, resolved) or a checkmark (✓) for feature confirmations
Bold is used for named agents, key outcomes, and the most critical phrase in a paragraph — not for decoration
Code snippets, command-line examples, and API references use monospace formatting on developer-facing pages
Numbered sequences (01, 02, 03) are used to show workflow steps and build the sense of a predictable, repeatable system
Section labels like 'The autonomous revenue system' and 'For sales reps and AEs' are used as eyebrow text above headlines to set context without burying it in the headline itself
CTAs use active verbs and concrete framing: 'Start Free,' 'Get API key,' 'See the use cases' — never 'Learn More' or 'Discover'
Avoid exclamation marks in product and feature copy; confidence comes from precision, not punctuation
Em dashes are used to separate a short declarative from its elaboration within a single sentence

# Compliance Rules

## Required Disclaimers

### Any page, ad, or content displaying logos of Okta, Google, Microsoft, Uber, Salesforce, Segment, Airbnb, BetterHelp, Learning Ally, WEX, Instapage, VeChain, or any other CIENCE heritage brand
**Text:** Brands shown are from the CIENCE campaign heritage that trained graph8. They are not current graph8 platform customers.
**When to use:** Whenever CIENCE heritage brand logos are used to establish credibility or social proof in graph8 marketing materials, landing pages, case studies, or ads

### Data Tax Calculator page, any ROI comparison content, pricing comparison tables, competitive displacement messaging
**Text:** Estimates based on published 2025 list prices. Your actual costs may vary based on contract size, negotiated discounts, and add-ons.
**When to use:** Any time graph8 publishes cost-comparison figures against competitor tools (ZoomInfo, Apollo, 6sense, Orum, Chili Piper, etc.) or estimates customer stack savings

### Pricing page, feature comparison tables, 'Unlimited' data claims in ads or landing pages
**Text:** Fair-use rate limits apply on all plans. They guard against scraping, not real GTM work.
**When to use:** Any time the words 'unlimited,' 'no cap,' or 'no monthly limit' appear adjacent to contact data, enrichment, or execution credits

### All sign-up CTAs, free trial landing pages, 'Start Free' buttons, and any signup flow entry point
**Text:** No credit card required. 500 free execution actions to start. By signing up you agree to graph8's Terms and Privacy Policy.
**When to use:** Every instance where a 'Start Free' or 'Sign Up' CTA is present — on homepage, product pages, role pages, pricing page, and paid ads

### Pricing page, all ad copy referencing the Team plan price, email campaigns mentioning pricing
**Text:** The $99/month Team plan price and feature inclusions are subject to change. Month-to-month, no contracts. Cancel anytime.
**When to use:** Any time the specific $99/month Team plan price is stated in marketing materials

### Startups page (graph8.com/startups), SMB page, any page referencing Deepgram, Rillet, Platzi, or Strike Social
**Text:** Startup operating patterns and customer logos on this page are example operating scenarios and reference patterns from the graph8 and CIENCE operating heritage.
**When to use:** When referencing startup or SMB customer scenarios that are illustrative rather than verified testimonials

### All product screenshots, UI mockups, demo environments, and any marketing material showing deal values, forecast numbers, or pipeline figures
**Text:** Weighted commit figures, pipeline amounts, and revenue figures shown are sample/illustrative data, not guaranteed outcomes.
**When to use:** Any time dollar amounts, pipeline figures, conversion rates, or revenue outcomes appear in UI screenshots or product demonstrations

### Enterprise page, security and compliance sections, any content referencing SOC 2 certification
**Text:** SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA for active enterprise evaluations. Contact your account executive.
**When to use:** When advertising SOC 2 Type II certification status to enterprise prospects

### Enterprise page, SSO and identity management feature descriptions, any content listing SCIM as a capability
**Text:** SCIM 2.0 provisioning is currently in pilot. Feature availability may vary.
**When to use:** Any time SCIM provisioning is listed as a product feature until general availability is confirmed

## Required Disclosures

### Privacy
- graph8 collects and processes personal data in accordance with its Privacy Policy (graph8.com/terms#privacy-policy). By signing up, users agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
- For EU customers, graph8 has Standard Contractual Clauses in place for cross-border data transfers. A Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is available on request.
- graph8 maintains a sub-processor list that is available on request, with material change notifications provided to enterprise customers.
- Right to erasure requests are processed across communication, recording, and revenue memory tables. Enterprise customers may request data deletion through their account executive.
- Call recording and AI voice agent interactions are subject to applicable wiretapping and call recording consent laws by jurisdiction. Users are responsible for obtaining required consent before recording calls in their jurisdiction.
- graph8 does not use customer data to train shared or general-purpose AI models. Customer data is isolated per organization at the database layer.
- GDPR-aware consent handling with audit logs and exportable records is available for EU-region customers.

### Pricing
- Execution credits are consumed only when graph8 performs real work: sends a message, places a call, books a meeting, runs an agent, or enriches a record. Browsing and searching never consumes credits.
- The Pay As You Go plan starts free and charges $0.05 per credit after the initial free allotment of 500 execution actions and 1,000 contact reveals.
- The MCP Unlimited plan is priced per user, not per organization. The Team plan is priced per organization with unlimited users.
- The Team plan ($99/month) includes 10,000 execution credits per month. Additional credits are available at published rates.
- Waterfall enrichment through third-party providers charges credits only on a successful match. Runs that return no match are free.
- Voice minutes (AI voice agents and dialer) are metered separately as execution credits. Rates are documented in the pricing page.
- The Data Tax Calculator comparison figures are illustrative estimates based on published 2025 list prices and may not reflect negotiated or enterprise contract rates for the tools compared.

### Data
- The graph8 buyer graph contains 700M+ verified B2B contacts and 100M+ companies. Contact data is sourced from multiple third-party providers and the CIENCE proprietary archive. Data accuracy and freshness may vary by record.
- graph8's Signals product processes approximately 2 billion buying signals per day. Signal data is aggregated from web activity, intent data co-ops, job posting feeds, technographic sources, and public data — not from private communications.
- Waterfall enrichment draws from multiple third-party data providers. graph8 does not guarantee 100% coverage or accuracy of enriched fields. Users should verify critical contact data before high-stakes outreach.
- Website visitor identification (Signals) identifies company-level visitors using IP resolution and device fingerprinting. Individual person-level identification depends on prior contact data availability and should not be assumed to be definitive.
- The Desktop application stores data locally on the user's device. Only data explicitly approved by the user is synced to the graph8 buyer graph.
- Agent Twins are trained on user-provided data: sent email history, call recordings, deal records, and LinkedIn profile data connected by the user. graph8 does not train Agent Twins on data the user has not explicitly connected.
- graph8's revenue memory is an append-only audit log. All agent and human actions are logged with actor, timestamp, and policy reference. This log is retained for the contracted period and exportable via API.

## Industry Regulations

### CAN-SPAM Act
**Applies to:** All email outreach sent through graph8 Sequencer, Inbox, Nurture, Newsletter, and Agent-initiated email campaigns targeting US recipients

**Requirements:**
- All commercial emails must include a working opt-out mechanism and honor unsubscribe requests within 10 business days
- Sender's physical postal address must be included in all commercial emails
- Email subject lines must not be deceptive or misleading
- Emails must be clearly identified as commercial messages where required
- Graph8 Sequencer and bulk email tools must maintain and honor suppression lists

**Impact on marketing:** All email campaigns, SDR Agent outreach, Newsletter broadcasts, and Nurture sequences must include compliant footers with unsubscribe links and physical address. Marketing materials promoting graph8's email capabilities must not encourage or facilitate CAN-SPAM violations.

### TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act)
**Applies to:** Voice AI dialer, AI Receptionist, parallel dialing, voicemail automation, and SMS outreach via graph8 Dialer and Inbox targeting US recipients

**Requirements:**
- Explicit prior written consent required before placing autodialed or pre-recorded calls to mobile phones
- Do-Not-Call (DNC) registry must be honored for all outbound voice campaigns
- SMS marketing messages require prior express written consent and must include opt-out instructions
- AI voice agents must disclose at the start of a call that the caller may be interacting with an AI if required by applicable law
- State-specific call recording consent rules (one-party vs. two-party states) must be followed by users of the Dialer and Voice AI products

**Impact on marketing:** Marketing for graph8 Dialer, Voice AI, Agent Twins voicemail, and SMS outreach features must not encourage users to bypass TCPA consent requirements. Sales materials must note that customers are responsible for obtaining required consents before using automated calling and texting features.

### GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation)
**Applies to:** All data processing involving EU/EEA residents — applicable to graph8's Data (Buyer Graph), Data Pipelines (CDP), Signals, Enrichment, and any outreach to EU contacts

**Requirements:**
- Legal basis for processing personal data must be established (legitimate interest, consent, contract, etc.) before using EU contact data in outreach
- Data subjects have rights of access, rectification, erasure, and portability — graph8 supports right-to-erasure requests across all data tables
- Data transfers outside the EEA require adequate safeguards — graph8 has Standard Contractual Clauses in place
- DPA (Data Processing Agreement) must be in place with enterprise customers processing EU personal data
- Privacy by design and data minimization principles apply to CDP data collection and enrichment workflows

**Impact on marketing:** Graph8 marketing targeting EU audiences must not promise capabilities that circumvent GDPR — e.g., mass cold outreach to EU contacts without lawful basis. EU-facing campaigns must reference graph8's GDPR compliance posture and DPA availability.

### CCPA / CPRA (California Consumer Privacy Act / California Privacy Rights Act)
**Applies to:** Processing of personal information of California residents via graph8's buyer graph, enrichment, visitor identification, and CDP products

**Requirements:**
- California residents have the right to know, delete, and opt out of the sale or sharing of their personal information
- Graph8's Privacy Policy must disclose categories of personal information collected and purposes of use
- Users of graph8's Signals and visitor identification must honor opt-out signals (e.g., Global Privacy Control) where applicable
- Do Not Sell or Share opt-out mechanism must be available

**Impact on marketing:** Marketing claims about graph8's visitor identification and contact data products must not imply that California consumer rights can be circumvented. Privacy Policy references must be current and accurate.

### FINRA Marketing Rules (FINRA Rules 2210, 2010)
**Applies to:** Marketing content created by graph8 Studio or sent via graph8 Sequencer/Agents targeting financial services firms or individuals in regulated securities industries

**Requirements:**
- Marketing copy for financial services firms must be fair, balanced, and not misleading
- Performance representations and ROI claims in content targeting FINRA-regulated firms require substantiation
- Approval queues before agent-initiated sends are required for content targeting regulated financial audiences
- State-by-state call recording rules apply to voice outreach targeting financial services contacts

**Impact on marketing:** Graph8's Fintech industry page and any outreach or Studio-generated content targeting FINRA-regulated buyers must be reviewed for compliance before deployment. Marketing materials must not suggest graph8 eliminates the need for compliance review of financial marketing content.

### HIPAA Considerations
**Applies to:** Graph8 Studio content generation, Sequencer outreach, and Data Pipelines used by healthtech or healthcare customers targeting PHI-adjacent audiences

**Requirements:**
- PHI (Protected Health Information) must not be included in outbound sales copy or stored in graph8's buyer graph fields without appropriate safeguards and BAA (Business Associate Agreement)
- Sequence rules in healthcare verticals must keep PHI out of outbound messaging
- Approval queues must be enabled before any agent-initiated send to healthcare contacts involving clinical or patient-adjacent content
- Consent and recording controls must be enforced for voice agents in healthcare contexts

**Impact on marketing:** Graph8 Healthtech marketing must not imply that the platform is pre-cleared for storing or transmitting PHI. Healthcare-focused campaigns must note that customer responsibility for HIPAA compliance is maintained and BAA availability should be confirmed via account executive.

### LinkedIn Platform Terms of Service
**Applies to:** Graph8 Sequencer LinkedIn outreach steps, Desktop LinkedIn automation, Agent Twins LinkedIn messaging, and Audience Syncs to LinkedIn Ads

**Requirements:**
- Automated LinkedIn messaging and connection requests must comply with LinkedIn's User Agreement and Professional Community Policies
- LinkedIn outreach volume limits must be respected to avoid account restrictions
- LinkedIn Audience Sync must use the official LinkedIn Marketing API and comply with LinkedIn Ads data policies
- Users are responsible for ensuring their LinkedIn outreach complies with LinkedIn's automation policies

**Impact on marketing:** Marketing for graph8's LinkedIn outreach and sequencing features must not promise capabilities that violate LinkedIn's platform terms. Copy should reference that users are responsible for LinkedIn compliance, and graph8 maintains integration through approved API channels.

### EU AI Act (Emerging — Monitor for Impact)
**Applies to:** Graph8's AI Agents, Agent Twins, Voice AI, AI Receptionist, and autonomous decision-making systems operating in or targeting EU markets

**Requirements:**
- AI systems interacting with EU individuals may require transparency disclosures identifying the interaction as AI-mediated
- High-risk AI use cases require documentation, human oversight mechanisms, and logging — graph8's revenue memory and human approval gates support this
- Organizations must maintain records of AI system use and be able to demonstrate human oversight — graph8's audit logs and approval gates address this requirement

**Impact on marketing:** EU-facing marketing for graph8's AI Agents, Voice AI, and Agent Twins should reference the platform's human-in-the-loop governance model and audit logging as compliance-enabling features. Do not make claims that graph8 is EU AI Act certified without legal review and certification confirmation.

## Approved Claims

### 700M+ verified B2B contacts and 100M+ companies, free to search on every plan

**Evidence:**
- Stated on graph8.com/platform/data, graph8.com/pricing, and across all product pages consistently
- Free search is confirmed in the pricing model: 'Search and browse buyers free on every plan'
- Contact count of 700M+ and company count of 100M+ are first-party platform claims from the product inventory

✅ **Correct usage:** graph8 gives your whole team access to 700M+ verified B2B contacts and 100M+ companies — free to search on every plan.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** graph8 has the world's largest B2B contact database with the most accurate data available.
**Expiration:** Revalidate quarterly — contact and company counts should be updated as the database grows

### graph8 processes approximately 2 billion buying signals per day, resolved to real people on the buyer graph

**Evidence:**
- Stated on graph8.com/platform/signals: 'graph8 brings every buying signal together, around 2 billion a day'
- Consistent with the product inventory: '30B intent signals' total processed
- Signal sources include visitor identification, intent data, hiring signals, job changes, and technographic changes

✅ **Correct usage:** graph8 Signals resolves approximately 2 billion buying signals per day to real people on the buyer graph, automatically triggering outreach when a buyer moves.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** graph8 tracks every buyer signal in real time with 100% accuracy and zero latency.
**Expiration:** Revalidate annually or upon significant architectural changes to the Signals product

### The Team plan ($99/month) includes unlimited users, every application, and 10,000 execution credits monthly with no seat fees

**Evidence:**
- Stated explicitly on graph8.com/pricing and graph8.com/ai-gtm pricing section
- Confirmed in product inventory: 'priced by execution usage rather than per-seat licenses'
- Pricing page lists Team plan at $99/mo with 'Unlimited users, no seat fees' and '10,000 execution credits a month'

✅ **Correct usage:** The graph8 Team plan covers your entire organization — unlimited users, every app, 10,000 execution credits — for $99/month. No seat fees, ever.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** graph8 is completely free for all users with no usage limits.
**Expiration:** Review whenever pricing is updated — this is a live pricing claim and must match the current pricing page

### graph8 is built on 10 years of real CIENCE B2B outbound campaign data across 2,500+ B2B brands

**Evidence:**
- Stated consistently across graph8.com homepage, roles pages, and gtm-services page
- CIENCE is the parent organization whose campaign heritage trained graph8's models
- Referenced on graph8.com: 'Grounded in 10 years of real CIENCE campaign data' and '2,500+ B2B brands run'

✅ **Correct usage:** graph8's agents and playbooks are trained on a decade of real B2B outbound data from CIENCE — across 2,500+ brands and millions of conversations — not synthetic data or generic AI models.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** graph8 has run campaigns for 2,500+ brands as a current customer list.

### graph8 is SOC 2 Type II certified

**Evidence:**

## Forbidden Terms

### Legal Reasons
- ❌ **guaranteed results** - graph8 cannot guarantee specific revenue outcomes, pipeline amounts, booking rates, or ROI. Results depend on customer implementation, ICP quality, market conditions, and usage patterns. All performance figures shown in marketing are illustrative samples.
- ❌ **100% accurate** - graph8's contact data, intent signals, visitor identification, and AI-generated outputs cannot be warranted as 100% accurate. Data accuracy varies by record, source, and recency.
- ❌ **unlimited accuracy** - No data vendor can claim unlimited or perfect accuracy. This would be a false claim about graph8's 700M+ contact database and enrichment products.
- ❌ **HIPAA compliant platform** - Graph8 does not position itself as a HIPAA-compliant platform. Healthcare customers using graph8 for outreach are responsible for their own HIPAA compliance. Do not claim platform-level HIPAA compliance without legal review and BAA framework confirmation.
- ❌ **FINRA approved** - Graph8 is not a FINRA-registered entity and does not hold FINRA approval. Marketing to financial services firms must not imply regulatory approval of the platform or its content.
- ❌ **scrape LinkedIn** - Explicitly violates LinkedIn's Terms of Service and constitutes a legally actionable claim. Graph8's LinkedIn integration operates via approved API channels and must not be characterized as scraping.
- ❌ **spam** - Never describe graph8's outreach capabilities as enabling spam or mass unsolicited messaging. Avoid this term entirely in reference to the Sequencer, Newsletter, Nurture, or Agent outreach features.
- ❌ **secretly record** - Graph8's call recording and Voice AI features must be used in compliance with applicable recording consent laws. Any language suggesting recordings are made without disclosure is legally prohibited.
- ❌ **current customer** - Do not describe CIENCE heritage brands (Okta, Google, Microsoft, Uber, Salesforce, Segment, etc.) as current graph8 platform customers. They are heritage campaign references from CIENCE. Using 'customer' language would constitute false advertising.
- ❌ **AI-powered [without qualification]** - The FTC has issued guidance on deceptive AI claims. All AI capability claims must be specific and accurate. 'AI-powered' as a standalone claim without describing the specific mechanism or capability is insufficiently substantiated.
- ❌ **fully autonomous** - Graph8 explicitly maintains human-in-the-loop controls and approval gates. Claiming full autonomy misrepresents the product's governance model and could create liability if autonomous agents cause harm without disclosed human oversight.
- ❌ **no data limits** - All graph8 plans have fair-use rate limits documented in the Terms. 'No data limits' as an unqualified claim contradicts the Terms of Service and published rate limit documentation.

### Competitive Reasons
- ❌ **better than [Competitor Name]** - Direct superiority claims without substantiated head-to-head testing data are legally risky and violate FTC guidelines on comparative advertising. Use feature-specific, substantiated comparisons only.
- ❌ **world's largest** - Graph8 cannot claim to have the world's largest contact database, signal network, or agent platform without independent verification and audited comparison. Competitors like ZoomInfo and Apollo claim comparable or larger database sizes.

### Brand Reasons
- ❌ **replaces your entire sales team** - graph8's core brand position is that AI agents amplify human reps, not replace them. The platform explicitly positions humans as winning the live moment. Claims suggesting full sales team replacement misrepresent the product and could trigger regulatory scrutiny around AI employment claims.
- ❌ **eliminates the need for human salespeople** - Contradicts graph8's foundational brand value ('Agents Do the Work, Humans Win the Moment'). Also legally and reputationally risky when targeting regulated industries.

**Can mention competitors:** Yes

**Rules:**
- All competitor mentions must be reviewed and approved by Legal before publication
- Comparison claims must be documented with source, date, and methodology
- Competitive content must remain factual, professional, and verifiable at time of publication
- Outdated competitive comparisons (older than 6 months) must be re-validated before reuse
- Do not use a competitor's trademarked name in paid search ad copy without legal clearance
- Comparative advertising must comply with the FTC's comparative advertising guidelines
- Any competitive battle cards or sales enablement materials referencing competitors require Legal and Product Marketing sign-off

**Approved comparisons:**
- ✅ Feature-by-feature comparisons backed by publicly available data
- ✅ Pricing comparisons using publicly listed prices with citation dates
- ✅ Third-party analyst report citations (e.g., G2, Gartner, Forrester)
- ✅ Customer-provided testimonials describing their switch from a named competitor

**Forbidden comparisons:**
- ❌ Unsubstantiated superiority claims (e.g., 'We are better than [Competitor]' without evidence)
- ❌ Disparaging or defamatory statements about competitor products or leadership
- ❌ Benchmark comparisons not conducted under controlled, reproducible conditions
- ❌ Claims implying a competitor's product is unsafe, fraudulent, or deceptive
- ❌ Using competitor logos or trademarked creative assets without written permission

## Review Process

### Always Review
- Any content making specific performance or ROI claims
- Comparative or competitive marketing materials (battle cards, landing pages, ads)

- Email campaigns targeting regulated industries (financial services, healthcare, legal)

### No Review Needed

- Internal training documents not distributed externally
- Direct 1:1 sales outreach using approved messaging templates

**Timeline:** 5 business days from submission for standard review

## Penalties

### Regulatory Penalties
- **GDPR:** Fines up to €20 million or 4% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher
- **CCPA:** Civil penalties up to $7,500 per intentional violation; $2,500 per unintentional violation
- **CAN-SPAM:** Penalties up to $53,088 per email in violation
- **TCPA:** Statutory damages of $500–$1,500 per call or text message in violation
- **FTC Act (Comparative Advertising):** Cease-and-desist orders, injunctions, and civil penalties for deceptive trade practices

### Company Policy
- First violation: Formal written warning issued to individual and their direct manager; mandatory compliance re-training required within 10 business days
- Second violation: Escalation to HR and department leadership; potential suspension of content publishing privileges pending investigation
- Third violation or willful misconduct: Termination of employment or contractor agreement; potential personal legal liability for damages caused
- Any violation resulting in a regulatory investigation must be immediately reported to the Legal team and CEO
- All non-compliant materials must be taken down within 2 hours of identification; failure to act promptly compounds disciplinary action
- Teams that publish unapproved competitive claims may lose access to competitive intelligence resources pending re-certification

data: The graph8 buyer graph contains 700M+ verified B2B contacts and 100M+ companies. Contact data is sourced from multiple third-party providers and the CIENCE proprietary archive. Data accuracy and freshness may vary by record.

graph8's Signals product processes approximately 2 billion buying signals per day. Signal data is aggregated from web activity, intent data co-ops, job posting feeds, technographic sources, and public data — not from private communications.

Waterfall enrichment draws from multiple third-party data providers. graph8 does not guarantee 100% coverage or accuracy of enriched fields. Users should verify critical contact data before high-stakes outreach.

Website visitor identification (Signals) identifies company-level visitors using IP resolution and device fingerprinting. Individual person-level identification depends on prior contact data availability and should not be assumed to be definitive.
The Desktop application stores data locally on the user's device. Only data explicitly approved by the user is synced to the graph8 buyer graph.

Agent Twins are trained on user-provided data: sent email history, call recordings, deal records, and LinkedIn profile data connected by the user. graph8 does not train Agent Twins on data the user has not explicitly connected.

graph8's revenue memory is an append-only audit log. All agent and human actions are logged with actor, timestamp, and policy reference. This log is retained for the contracted period and exportable via API.
pricing: Execution credits are consumed only when graph8 performs real work: sends a message, places a call, books a meeting, runs an agent, or enriches a record. Browsing and searching never consumes credits.
The Pay As You Go plan starts free and charges $0.05 per credit after the initial free allotment of 500 execution actions and 1,000 contact reveals.
The MCP Unlimited plan is priced per user, not per organization. The Team plan is priced per organization with unlimited users.
The Team plan ($99/month) includes 10,000 execution credits per month. Additional credits are available at published rates.
Waterfall enrichment through third-party providers charges credits only on a successful match. Runs that return no match are free.
Voice minutes (AI voice agents and dialer) are metered separately as execution credits. Rates are documented in the pricing page.
The Data Tax Calculator comparison figures are illustrative estimates based on published 2025 list prices and may not reflect negotiated or enterprise contract rates for the tools compared.
privacy: graph8 collects and processes personal data in accordance with its Privacy Policy (graph8.com/terms#privacy-policy). By signing up, users agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
For EU customers, graph8 has Standard Contractual Clauses in place for cross-border data transfers. A Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is available on request.
graph8 maintains a sub-processor list that is available on request, with material change notifications provided to enterprise customers.
Right to erasure requests are processed across communication, recording, and revenue memory tables. Enterprise customers may request data deletion through their account executive.

Call recording and AI voice agent interactions are subject to applicable wiretapping and call recording consent laws by jurisdiction. Users are responsible for obtaining required consent before recording calls in their jurisdiction.
graph8 does not use customer data to train shared or general-purpose AI models. Customer data is isolated per organization at the database layer.
GDPR-aware consent handling with audit logs and exportable records is available for EU-region customers.
